### 575. Stop the cross-phase ceiling check reading a stop-word as a unit and false-positiving on N-of-M prose
- **Status**: [NOT STARTED]
- **Task Type**: meta
- **Topic**: core-agent-system
- **Dependencies**: None

**Description**: SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/** (never a deployed .claude/** tree, which is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). Resolve it with `jq -r '.extensions.core.source_dir' .claude-extensions.json` (source_dir is a PER-EXTENSION key, not a top-level one). Edit at the path mirroring the deployed one, then REDEPLOY via deploy-headless.sh. No task-number references and no record-versioning language in any file landing under agent-system/** (rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md, rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md); both are permitted in this description and elsewhere in specs/**.

ORIGIN: Conclusion stage (channel b, agent-system change request) of an /orchestrate invocation, user-approved at the lead level and dispatched to the meta builder for task creation only. CITATION: task 420, entry iss_1794090946368_48ofpk in specs/420_warn_plan_size_exceeds_cycle_budget/issues.jsonl (class tooling-or-harness-defect, severity minor, plan phase, resolution open, suggested_channel agent_system -- this routing agrees with the hint). That entry records TWO defects; this record owns the FIRST only. See the SECOND DEFECT IS ALREADY OWNED section below.

THE DEFECT, reproduced at creation time and not inferred. validate-artifact.sh's advisory cross-phase ceiling-consistency check extracts a per-phase quantity estimate from a phase's **Scope Hypothesis** block with `grep -oE '[0-9]+(-[0-9]+)?[[:space:]]+(added[[:space:]]+)?[A-Za-z]+'` and takes the match's TRAILING WORD as the unit noun. Ordinary statistical prose of the shape "N of M <noun>" therefore yields the unit word "of": the token "92 of" matches, "of" becomes the unit, and the check then hunts a ceiling citation and a conformance assertion for the unit "of". Both scans find one trivially, because "of" occurs in nearly every line of English prose that also contains a digit and one of the words ceiling, limit, budget, or cap -- the three-condition gate the check's own comment calls "deliberately strict to keep false positives low" collapses entirely when the unit is a stop-word. The ceiling value is then read as the first integer on whatever line matched, producing a nonsensical bound.

EXACT REPRODUCTION (re-run it before editing; it is cheap and it is the failing-first case):
  - Take a plan that validates clean. Appending the clause "Measured: 92 of 155 run_sut call sites already pass the fixture root explicitly." to one phase's Scope Hypothesis line was sufficient.
  - `validate-artifact.sh <plan> plan` then emits: `[WARN] Per-phase of estimates (phases:5) sum to 92 (incl. baseline 0), past the cited 0-of ceiling this plan also asserts it stays within`.
  - Unmodified, the same plan reports `[PASS] plan artifact is valid (0 warning(s))`.
  - Under `--strict` the same false positive turns the run into `[FAIL] 0 error(s), 1 warning(s)`, because this check rides the pre-existing `total_issues = errors + warnings` branch. A false positive is therefore gate-blocking in strict mode, not merely noisy.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SEVERITY SUGGESTS. The originating dispatch worked around it by rephrasing its own prose to drop the N-of-M shape. That leaves the checker defect unfixed and recurring for any author who writes a legitimate N-of-M statistic -- and it carries the same bad incentive the sentinel-path-set record names: it pressures authors to write worse, less precise prose to satisfy a checker rather than fixing the checker. Two further consequences: the check's documented promotion criterion in context/formats/plan-format.md is "promote the warning to an error once a default-mode sweep of every non-terminal plan under specs/ shows zero plans newly warning", so false positives on ordinary prose indefinitely block a promotion that is otherwise earned; and if the check were promoted with this hole open, honestly-worded plans would hard-fail. Note that plan-format.md's own Enforcement level subsection contains the phrase "0 of 14 non-terminal plans under specs/" -- the governing document is itself written in the shape its checker misreads.

THE DESIGN TENSION, which must be resolved deliberately rather than by accident. plan-format.md's Cross-phase ceiling consistency obligation is deliberately unit-generic: "a line count, a file count, a token budget, or any other countable dimension", and its worked example states the obligation holds "regardless of which linter or unit the ceiling happens to come from". So the fix must NOT be a whitelist of known units such as line and file -- that would silently narrow the stated obligation. The fix must exclude non-units while keeping the unit vocabulary open.

THE ASK:
(1) Stop a stop-word from ever being read as a unit noun. At minimum "of" must be excluded; enumerate the closed set of function words that can legitimately follow a bare integer in English prose (of, in, to, out, and, or, than, per, through, across, from, by, with, as, at, is, are, was, were, the, a, an) and decide the predicate deliberately rather than patching the single observed token. State the chosen set and its reasoning.
(2) Recognize the N-of-M shape itself as a ratio rather than a quantity estimate. "92 of 155 run_sut call sites" states a proportion over an existing population; it is not a per-phase quantity this phase will add, so it must not enter the accumulation at all -- not under the unit "of", and not under the unit "sites" either. Decide and state whether the M-side noun is admitted, excluded, or admitted only outside an N-of-M context.
(3) Keep the check's existing deliberate lossiness posture intact: its comment records that a miss is a missed warning and never a suppressed stricter finding, and that it must not be promoted to log_error as part of an unrelated change. Honor both. A narrower extraction that misses a real contradiction is acceptable; a false positive on honest prose is not.
(4) Leave the three-condition gate's structure alone unless the ruling in (1) and (2) genuinely requires changing it, and say which if it does.

VERIFY:
(1) Extend agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/test-validate-artifact.sh with fixtures pinning: (a) the exact reproduction above warning ZERO times, demonstrated failing-first against the unmodified source-store script; (b) a genuine same-unit contradiction in the shape plan-format.md's worked example describes -- per-phase line estimates summing past a cited line ceiling while the plan asserts conformance -- still warning, so the fix is a narrowing of the predicate and not a disabling of the check; (c) each function word in the chosen stop-word set exercised at least once; (d) an N-of-M clause whose M-side noun coincides with a real unit the same plan also cites a ceiling for, behaving as the ruling in (2) decided.
(2) Re-run the default-mode sweep that produced the promotion criterion's residue figure and report the re-measured count rather than carrying the recorded one forward. If the residue is now zero, say so and say explicitly whether the promotion criterion is thereby met -- but do NOT promote the check in this task; promotion is its own decision with its own consumers.
(3) Update the obligation and Enforcement level subsections in context/formats/plan-format.md only insofar as the implemented predicate changed what authors can rely on. Do not restate the implementation there.
(4) Name covering suites from an actual suite_selection_select run over the touched paths, not from assertion.

THE SECOND DEFECT IN THE CITED ENTRY IS ALREADY OWNED -- DO NOT WORK IT HERE. That entry's second half records that suite_selection_select returns a LARGER set for a multi-path call than the union of per-path calls over the same paths. That is the same mechanism the open record fix_validateartifactsh_tier_justification_false_po (titled for the Tier Justification false positive from sentinel path-set membership) already owns: a path set containing one sentinel-mapped member escalates the WHOLE call to __FULL_SWEEP__, so the sentinel member dominates every non-sentinel member. Measured here independently at creation time: `suite_selection_select context/contracts/phase-closure.md scripts/lib/suite-selection-lib.sh` returns `__FULL_SWEEP__`, while the second path alone returns `test-run-all-selection.sh` and `test-validate-artifact.sh` -- an author composing a Tier Justification from per-path runs and discarding the sentinel line therefore under-names real covering suites, which is exactly the observed under-naming. That record's point (1) also settles the question of which result is correct: the compositional union, with __FULL_SWEEP__ kept as a floor contributed by its own member rather than a ceiling imposed on the set. This record creates no duplicate of it and must not edit suite-selection-lib.sh.

TERRITORY. scripts/validate-artifact.sh and scripts/tests/test-validate-artifact.sh are contended by four open records: the sentinel-path-set Tier Justification fix, the reversed-argument-order fault, the CARRIED-UNVERIFIED mark validation record, and the baseline-relative gate criteria record. context/formats/plan-format.md is contended more widely still. No dependency edge is filed, matching the explicit, stated treatment both the sentinel-path-set record and the argument-order record already give this exact file pair: subject matter is disjoint -- a different check in a 677-line script -- so the overlap is mechanical only. Re-check at admission time and batch rather than exclude. In particular, if the sentinel-path-set record is admitted alongside this one, run them in one batch: they touch the same two files and the same script, and serialized batching is the sanctioned response to shared territory.

NON-GOALS: no promotion of this check from warning to error; no edit to scripts/lib/suite-selection-lib.sh or tests/test-run-all-selection.sh; no change to the Verification Tier or Files to modify checks that share the same per-phase loop; no change to the argument-parsing guard sequence; no hand-authored file under any deployed .claude/** tree.

### 574. Correct the cycle-budget contract to state shared-pool semantics wherever remaining budget is described
- **Status**: [NOT STARTED]
- **Task Type**: meta
- **Topic**: core-agent-system
- **Dependencies**: None

**Description**: SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/** (never a deployed .claude/** tree, which is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). Resolve it with `jq -r '.extensions.core.source_dir' .claude-extensions.json` (source_dir is a PER-EXTENSION key, not a top-level one). Edit at the path mirroring the deployed one, then REDEPLOY via deploy-headless.sh. No task-number references and no record-versioning language in any file landing under agent-system/** (rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md, rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md); both are permitted in this description and elsewhere in specs/**.

ORIGIN: Conclusion stage (channel b, agent-system change request) of an /orchestrate invocation, user-approved at the lead level and dispatched to the meta builder for task creation only. CITATION: task 420, entry iss_1794090304994_akHoH2 in specs/420_warn_plan_size_exceeds_cycle_budget/issues.jsonl (class requirements-gap, severity minor, research phase, resolution open, suggested_channel agent_system -- this routing agrees with the hint). Read that entry's what_happened before editing.

THIS IS A DOCUMENTATION AND CONTRACT CORRECTION, NOT A BEHAVIOR CHANGE. Nothing about how the budget is enforced is in question or in scope. Confirm the current behavior by reading the code before writing a single word of corrected prose, and state in the summary what the re-derivation found.

THE MECHANISM, verified by direct read of the source store at creation time (line numbers move; re-derive before editing):
- scripts/orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh sets `per_task_max_cycles=5`, or `13` under --hard, then computes `batch_cycle_budget=$(( ${#task_args[@]} * per_task_max_cycles ))` -- every task in the batch CONTRIBUTES its allotment to ONE pool that all of them draw from. There is no `min(..., 25)` clamp anywhere in the computation.
- The eligibility gate, and the plan-size advisory that deliberately mirrors it, both read `.batch_cycle_budget` against the SUM of `.cycle_counts` (`[.cycle_counts[]? // 0] | add // 0`), never a single task's own count against its own slice.
- Consequence: a task may spend more cycles than its own contribution when a sibling needs fewer. The pool, not the task, is the bound. A single-task invocation is the batch-of-one special case where a per-task reading happens to coincide with the pool reading.

THE HAZARD, stated as the originating entry states it: a future plan or implementation phase that naively implements a per-task subtraction would silently disagree with the mechanism that actually enforces the cap. The disagreement would not surface as an error -- both readings produce a plausible integer, and they coincide exactly in the batch-of-one case most dispatches exercise. That is what makes the misframing worth correcting rather than tolerating.

MEASURED RESIDUE. docs/architecture/orchestrate-state-machine.md's MAX_CYCLES Enforcement section already names the shared pool explicitly and correctly; it is not the gap. The gap is everywhere else, and it has two distinct shapes:

(1) PER-TASK FRAMING OF A POOL STOP. The state-transition table near the top of orchestrate-state-machine.md gives the stop condition as `cycle_count >= MAX_CYCLES`, a single counter against a single bound. The same file's "On cycle limit" prose reports "Task {N} reached MAX_CYCLES limit", attributing to one task an exhaustion the pool incurred collectively. docs/guides/user-guide.md's Cycle Budgets subsection says "the task is left [PARTIAL]" on reaching the cap, with no indication that siblings' spending is what reached it. commands/orchestrate.md's termination list and its MAX_CYCLES Reached entry carry the same per-task reading.

(2) A FORMULA THE CODE DOES NOT IMPLEMENT. Five places state `MAX_CYCLES_MT = min(task_count * 5, 25)`: docs/guides/user-guide.md, docs/architecture/orchestrate-state-machine.md's own MT Exit Conditions section, context/patterns/task-lock.md, scripts/task-lock.sh's header comment, and scripts/reap-session-runtime-files.sh's header comment. The implemented value is `ntasks * per_task_max_cycles` with no clamp, and `per_task_max_cycles` is 13 under --hard, so the stated formula is wrong in base mode for any batch wider than five tasks and wrong under --hard at every width. Note that orchestrate-state-machine.md therefore contradicts ITSELF: its MAX_CYCLES Enforcement snippet gives `BATCH_CYCLE_BUDGET=$(( ntasks * PER_TASK_CYCLES ))` while its MT Exit Conditions section gives the clamped formula. Also note that orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's own pool comment appeals to "MAX_TASKS bounds the pool by construction" while defining no MAX_TASKS -- establish where, if anywhere, a batch-width cap is actually enforced before repeating that claim or deleting it.

THE ASK:
(1) Wherever remaining budget, the budget bound, or the stop condition is described, name the pool semantics explicitly: the bound is the batch-wide pool, the quantity tested is the SUM of every batched task's cycle_counts, and a single task's own count is not the gate. Keep the batch-of-one reduction stated where a reader of a single-task example would otherwise generalize wrongly.
(2) Settle the `min(task_count * 5, 25)` claim against the implementation and make all five sites agree with whatever the code actually does. If a width cap exists somewhere, cite where and keep the clamp. If it does not, remove the clamp from the prose rather than adding one to the code -- this task changes no behavior.

### 571. Invalidate an in-flight dispatch whose dispatch_seq has been superseded, at consumption time
- **Status**: [NOT STARTED]
- **Task Type**: meta
- **Topic**: agent-system
- **Dependencies**: Task 450, Task 487, Task 518

**Description**: SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/** (never a deployed .claude/** tree, which is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). Edit at the path mirroring the deployed one, then REDEPLOY via deploy-headless.sh. No task-number references and no record-versioning language in any file landing under agent-system/** (rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md, rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md); both are permitted in this description and elsewhere in specs/**.

ORIGIN: conclusion stage (channel b, agent-system change request) of an /orchestrate run over BimodalLogic tasks 893 and 901, session sess_1794246177_f0f988. User-approved at the orchestrate-lead level and dispatched to the meta builder for task creation only. FILED HERE, NOT IN BIMODALLOGIC, per the mis-siting correction recorded under this repo's #390.

SEVERITY: costly. No corruption resulted -- the receiving agent refused on its own initiative -- but a full plan dispatch was spent on a task that had already finished, and the refusal depended on the agent noticing an output-path collision rather than on any contract.

## The defect

A dispatch whose dispatch_seq has been superseded is still deliverable, and is still delivered.

MEASURED: a plan dispatch at dispatch_seq 2 reached a planner-agent after its task had completed its entire lifecycle. At delivery time the loop guard already recorded `dispatch_seq_counter` 3; the plan file was marked [COMPLETED] with all four phases closed; and both `.return-meta.json` and `.orchestrator-handoff.json` carried `dispatch_seq` 3 with `status: implemented`. Every piece of state needed to recognise the dispatch as superseded was already on disk and already consistent.

The planner behaved correctly: it refused to write any artifact, because its assigned output path collided exactly with the plan that had already been executed, and it left a report instead. That refusal is a fortunate consequence of a path collision, not an enforced contract -- a dispatch whose output path happened not to collide would have proceeded and overwritten live state.

## Where the gap is

dispatch_seq freshness is checked only on the RETURN side. The closed record under this repo's #143 built `orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh` around an mtime staleness gate plus a dispatch_seq identity gate on the handoff read, and gave `orchestrate-recover-outcome.sh` the same identity check; #33 gave `.orchestrator-handoff.json` per-dispatch identity in the first place. Read both records' artifacts before re-deriving any of this. Both operate on what comes BACK. Nothing validates identity at dispatch CONSUMPTION time, so the loop guard can know the counter has advanced while an in-flight dispatch carrying the old seq remains perfectly deliverable.

## Scope

Add an identity check an agent performs before doing any work, and give it a defined no-op outcome. Shape, to be settled during the work:

- The dispatch file written by `scripts/orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh` already carries an Identity section with a `dispatch_seq:` line; the receiving agent already echoes that value verbatim into its handoff and return-meta. Extend that contract so the agent first COMPARES it against the live `.orchestrator-loop-guard` `dispatch_seq_counter` and the task's persisted status.
- On a superseded dispatch, abort as an explicit no-op: write a terminal return-meta naming the supersession, author no artifact, and make no status transition. Define how postflight classifies that outcome so a correct no-op is not then recorded as a work failure.
- The check belongs wherever it cannot be skipped. Prose in each dispatched agent's own file is the cheapest route and matches how `dispatch_seq` echoing is already specified; a script-side preflight the dispatch body invokes is the stronger route. Decide which, and say why in the record.

## Hard constraints

- MUST NOT weaken the existing return-side staleness and identity gates.
- MUST NOT make a legitimately re-dispatched same-seq retry look superseded: the stall/strand re-prompt relay deliberately re-dispatches at the SAME dispatch_seq, and that path must keep working.
- A superseded dispatch MUST NOT write an artifact, and MUST NOT rely on an output-path collision to stop itself.

## Durable evidence anchors

- BimodalLogic specs/893_lcu_until_form_schema_ztime_validity/issues.jsonl: iss_1794254863132_W2Q6md
- the refusing agent's own report: specs/893_lcu_until_form_schema_ztime_validity/stale-dispatch-2-plan-report.md in BimodalLogic
- closed prior art to read first: this repo's #143 and #33

## Overlapping open file territory

#450 (validate_settled_route_before_dispatch) declares orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh, its test, skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md and handoff-schema.md -- a near-complete overlap with this record. #487 (identical_dispatch_halt_despite_phase_progress) declares orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh. #518 (handoff_blockers_admission_contract_at_authoring_sites) declares all four dispatched-agent files and handoff-schema.md. All three are declared as dependencies so batch admission orders rather than parallelizes them.

### 570. Stop the stall signal firing on commits it cannot attribute to the dispatch under judgement
- **Status**: [NOT STARTED]
- **Task Type**: meta
- **Topic**: agent-system
- **Dependencies**: Task 519, Task 543

**Description**: SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/** (never a deployed .claude/** tree, which is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). Edit at the path mirroring the deployed one, then REDEPLOY via deploy-headless.sh. No task-number references and no record-versioning language in any file landing under agent-system/** (rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md, rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md); both are permitted in this description and elsewhere in specs/**.

ORIGIN: conclusion stage (channel b, agent-system change request) of an /orchestrate run over BimodalLogic tasks 893 and 901, session sess_1794246177_f0f988. User-approved at the orchestrate-lead level and dispatched to the meta builder for task creation only. FILED HERE, NOT IN BIMODALLOGIC: an agent-system change belongs in the repository that owns the source store, per the mis-siting correction recorded under this repo's #390.

SEVERITY: costly. The signal is advisory, so it changes no verdict, but a false firing routes a dead dispatch into the one-re-prompt relay and spends a cycle re-prompting an agent that produced nothing.

## The defect

`stall_suspected` fires for a dispatch that did no work at all, because its commit probe attributes nothing.

In `scripts/orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh` the trigger is a conjunction of (phase is plan or implement) AND (no outcome recovered) AND (at least one commit touching the task directory since `dispatch_start_ts`). The commit half is a bare existence count:

    stall_commit_count=$(git -C "${SKILL_REPO_ROOT:-.}" log --oneline \
      --since="@${dispatch_start_ts}" -- "$TASK_DIR" 2>/dev/null | grep -c . )

Nothing ties a counted commit to the dispatch under judgement. Two distinct provenances therefore trip it:

1. A commit from an EARLIER dispatch_seq whose own phase commit landed inside this dispatch's window. This is the measured case: a plan dispatch died of an API transport error (ESERVFAIL) having authored nothing, and `stall_suspected=true` was raised on the strength of one commit carried over from the previous phase.
2. Postflight's OWN per-task commit. The script's `rd_stall_*` record-time block already documents this asymmetry in its own comment -- it states that WORK (i)'s per-task commit "lands strictly between this point and that later computation, so a commit this block sees here is necessarily the DISPATCHED AGENT's own work, never postflight's". The canonical `stall_suspected` computation runs AFTER that commit and carries no equivalent guarantee.

## Why the existing comment does not already cover this

Read `stall_suspected`'s own DELIBERATE NON-WIDENING comment before editing; it is adjacent enough to misjudge. That comment refuses to OR a stale-dispatch_seq signal INTO the trigger as an additional disjunct, on the ground that a stale seq cannot distinguish an abandoned wrap-up from an instant death. This record asks for the opposite operation on the other half of the conjunction: NARROW the existing commit term by attributing each counted commit, so a commit that cannot belong to this dispatch stops satisfying it. That strengthens the discrimination the comment exists to protect rather than dissolving it, and the non-widening ruling stands unchanged.

## Scope

Decide the attribution mechanism and implement it. Candidates, not a mandate: key the probe on the commit message's own task/phase marker; bound the window below by this dispatch's own start rather than relying on `--since` alone; or compare against the commit set already present at dispatch start and count only the delta. Whatever is chosen must also close the postflight-own-commit leak, or state in the code why that leak is acceptable at the canonical site when the record-time site took care to avoid it.

## Hard constraints

- MUST preserve the commit-gated conjunction as the field's only discrimination (see the DELIBERATE NON-WIDENING comment).
- MUST NOT make a genuine abandoned wrap-up stop firing: the measured symptom this field exists to catch is an agent that committed real work and then ended its turn on an unresolved background wait.
- `stranded_suspected` is a lexically separate field and is NOT in scope; do not merge the two.

## Durable evidence anchors

- BimodalLogic specs/893_lcu_until_form_schema_ztime_validity/issues.jsonl: iss_1794248764333_aYwsfu, iss_1794248927414_qePymU
- detecting site: scripts/orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh, the `stall_suspected` block

## Overlapping open file territory

This repo's #519 (infra_exempt_transport_error_dispatch_deaths) is the sibling half of the same measured misdiagnosis -- it owns the `transport_error` + `status=in_progress` cycle-charge question and may restructure the branch whose message this field's corroboration feeds. #543 owns the stall/strand re-prompt REMEDY TEXT in the same script and the same test file. Both are declared as dependencies so batch admission orders rather than parallelizes them. #551, #501 and #472 also declare this script; no edge is asserted for those, the overlap is recorded so admission can order it.

CITATION: the plan-defect cluster in BimodalLogic:specs/902_reassess_lplus_ztime_nogo_cslib_omega_automata/issues.jsonl -- entries iss_1794232152215_azaeZh, iss_1794232152239_LNegjQ, iss_1794232478589_ECQN4Z, iss_1794232478611_zThTVn, iss_1794232627189_lpNGZD. The load-bearing one is iss_1794232478589_ECQN4Z. Read these before editing; the cluster as a whole is the evidence that unsatisfiable and vacuous verification criteria are a recurring authoring failure in that session, not a single slip.

THE DEFECT. The dependency-cycle check is Check D5, inside validate-state.sh's --deep block. A bare `bash .claude/scripts/validate-state.sh` runs only the base-mode checks, NEVER reaches D5, and exits 0 either way. Nothing in the usage text a caller reads says so. Measured: a plan specified "validate-state.sh exits 0, cycle check included" as a phase verification criterion with a bare invocation. That criterion WOULD HAVE PASSED VACUOUSLY. Re-run as `validate-state.sh --deep` it reported 19 passed / 19 warnings / 0 failed, exit 0, with "No dependency cycles detected among active_projects" explicitly observed -- so the claim happened to be true, and the criterion that asserted it was still worthless. A verification criterion that cannot fail is worse than no criterion, because it manufactures confidence that nothing checked.

THE ASK, two surfaces:
(1) validate-state.sh's own usage output and --help must state that the dependency-cycle check requires --deep and is NOT run in base mode. The script's doc header already distinguishes base from --deep checks; the usage text a caller actually reads does not. Additionally, make the base-mode summary output name that deep checks were not run, so a reader of the OUTPUT -- not only a reader of the flag list -- can tell that a cycle check did not happen. The output-side notice is the part that would actually have caught the cited plan, since the plan author read output, not usage.
(2) Plan-authoring guidance (context/formats/plan-format.md, with the planner agent's verification-criteria guidance pointing at it rather than restating it) must state that a cycle-check verification criterion MUST specify --deep, naming the vacuous-pass failure mode as the reason. State the rule once; point to it from the second surface.

GENERALIZE EXACTLY ONE STEP, NO FURTHER. While here, check whether any OTHER check a plan is likely to cite as a verification criterion is likewise gated behind a flag that a bare invocation never reaches. The --strict and --archive modes are the obvious candidates, and the script's doc header notes that no current caller passes --strict. Name whichever ones are real in the same guidance sentence. Do NOT restructure the flag layout and do NOT promote D5 into base mode: the fix is honest documentation of a real gate, not a change to what the gate is or what it costs.

VERIFY: `validate-state.sh --help` states the --deep requirement for the cycle check; a base-mode run's output names that deep checks did not run; plan-format.md states that a cycle-check criterion must specify --deep and names the vacuous-pass failure mode; the planner agent points at that rule without duplicating it; and a grep of the guidance surfaces shows no remaining example specifying a bare validate-state.sh as a cycle-check criterion. Extend the existing validate-state.sh suite with a fixture pinning the base-mode "deep checks not run" notice.

TERRITORY AND ORDERING. This record declares context/formats/plan-format.md and agents/planner-agent.md, both also declared by the baseline-relative-gate-criteria record and the evidence-discipline record in this backlog. The baseline-relative record edits the same verification-criteria guidance in the same two files, so a dependency edge is FILED on it: land it first and write this rule into the structure it leaves behind, rather than having two records edit that guidance concurrently. Its subject is distinct (an absolute criterion over a gate carrying standing pre-existing findings, versus a criterion naming a check that a bare invocation cannot reach), so this is a serialization edge, not a duplication claim. The evidence-discipline record's overlap is on different sections of the same files; no edge filed, re-check at admission.

NON-GOALS. No hand-authored file under any deployed .claude/** tree; no change to which checks run in which mode and no promotion of D5 into base mode; no attempt to fix the pre-existing legacy file_scope warnings the deep run reports; no new validation script.

THE DEFECT. Task descriptions and composed dispatch context cite prior art by its LIVE task-directory path, specs/{NNN}_{SLUG}/.... The /todo archival step MOVES that directory to specs/archive/{NNN}_{SLUG}/, so every such citation becomes a dead path the moment the cited task is archived. Measured instance: a dispatch cited prior art at specs/736_.../summaries/01_cslib-omega-automata-survey-summary.md while the real path was specs/archive/736_cslib_omega_automata_survey_and_e3_reopen_check/summaries/01_cslib-omega-automata-survey-summary.md.

WHY THE MEASURED COST UNDERSTATES THE DEFECT. In the cited run the cost was one extra find call, because that agent searched. The failure mode that matters is the silent one: a dispatched agent that reads the named path, gets nothing, and proceeds on a thinner evidence base than the composer intended -- without ever reporting that the prior art it was pointed at was unreadable. The citation looks authoritative and resolves to nothing. This is systematic, not incidental: every prior-art citation in every description ages into this state as its cited task archives.

WHY THIS IS CHEAP. The archive-awareness rule is already defined as executable data in agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/lib/task-lookup-lib.sh, whose task_lookup_dir <project_number> <project_name> <repo_root> resolves active-then-archive-then-new, and whose own header states that every consumer sources it rather than hand-copying the jq. What is missing is a resolver for a LITERAL specs/{NNN}_{SLUG}/... PATH STRING -- the form that actually appears in prose -- plus its use at the surfaces that compose prior-art paths into a dispatch.

THE ASK:
(1) Add the string-path resolver as a function in task-lookup-lib.sh itself, not as a second copy of the archive-normalization rule anywhere else. It takes a literal specs/{NNN}_{SLUG}/... path and returns the path that EXISTS, resolving the directory half through the same active-then-archive precedence task_lookup_dir already implements while preserving the remainder of the path verbatim.
(2) Add a resolve-on-compose step: before a prior-art path is emitted into a dispatch prompt, resolve it and emit the resolved path.
(3) Where a path cannot be resolved, say so EXPLICITLY in the composed context rather than passing an unverified path through. (4) Enumerate the composition surfaces by grepping the source store for literal specs/ path interpolation in the dispatch-composing scripts, skills and agents, and wire each one. Do not special-case a single caller. Re-derive the surface list at implement time rather than trusting any list written into this description.

Confirm by grep that no second copy of the archive-normalization rule was introduced.

### 564. Fix validate-artifact.sh Tier Justification false positive from sentinel path-set membership
- **Status**: [NOT STARTED]
- **Task Type**: meta
- **Topic**: core-agent-system
- **Dependencies**: Task 505

**Description**: SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/** (never a deployed .claude/** tree, which is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). Edit at the path mirroring the deployed one, then REDEPLOY via deploy-headless.sh. No task-number references and no record-versioning language in any file landing under agent-system/** (rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md, rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md); both are permitted in this description and elsewhere in specs/**.

ORIGIN: Conclusion stage (channel b, agent-system change) of an /orchestrate invocation over BimodalLogic:#902 (re-assess the L-plus ZTime completeness NO-GO against CSLib omega-automata), user-approved at the lead level and dispatched to the meta builder for task creation only. FILED HERE, NOT IN BIMODALLOGIC: an agent-system change belongs in the repository that owns the source store, matching the standing precedent set by the records for the settled-user-decision route and baseline-relative gate criteria, both filed here from this same channel. BimodalLogic carries only the deployed, disposable .claude/ tree; a record filed there whose edit targets resolve only under this store cannot be worked or committed from there, which is why the audit-verdict argv record filed there was abandoned as mis-sited by owner direction, and why the mis-sited-delta migration records exist.

RESOLVING THE SOURCE STORE, because the originating session got this wrong and the correction is load-bearing: source_dir is a PER-EXTENSION key, not a top-level one. Resolve with `jq -r '.extensions.core.source_dir' .claude-extensions.json`, which yields /home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/core. The originating issue entry read the top level, found no source_dir, and concluded the source store was unreachable; that conclusion is FALSE -- the store exists and every file named below was confirmed present at filing time.

CITATION: entry iss_1794231891214_RHng07 in BimodalLogic:specs/902_reassess_lplus_ztime_nogo_cslib_omega_automata/issues.jsonl (class: tooling false positive, severity minor, plan phase, resolution worked_around). Read that entry's what_happened before editing.

THE DEFECT. suite_selection_select returns the __FULL_SWEEP__ sentinel for any path SET that CONTAINS a sentinel-mapped path. A set's sentinel membership therefore overrides all of its non-sentinel members. Measured consequence: a plan phase whose "Files to modify" listed the plan's own bookkeeping path alongside a real narrow target (specs/ROADMAP.md) had its selector output collapse to the sentinel, so validate-artifact.sh's Tier Justification check warned that the phase's honest two-suite claim was unsupported. A narrow, truthful claim read as fabricated.

WHAT WAS DONE INSTEAD, AND WHY IT MUST NOT BECOME THE PRACTICE. The cited plan excluded the plan-notes bookkeeping path from that phase's "Files to modify" and said so explicitly in the Scope Hypothesis; the plan then validated with 0 warnings. That is a per-plan workaround with a bad incentive: it pressures authors to UNDER-DECLARE real file scope to satisfy a checker, which degrades exactly the file_scope data that territory contention and the overlap predicates depend on.

THIS IS A SECOND, DISTINCT ESCALATION MODE -- NOT THE ONE THE NON-CORE SELECTION RECORD OWNS. That record (planned, this backlog, titled for making covering-suite selection resolve a non-core extension's source-store scripts) addresses a path that is NOT MAPPED AT ALL because its extension's scripts tree is not walked. This record addresses a path that IS mapped, in a set alongside another mapped path, where the sentinel member dominates the non-sentinel member. Both are false sweep escalations in the same library; the causes are disjoint. That record's own point (3) states the shared principle this one also honours: keep __FULL_SWEEP__ as the honest answer where no suite covers a path; the defect is a false escalation for a path that DOES have a covering suite, never the sentinel itself.

THE ASK -- make set semantics compositional rather than sentinel-dominated:
(1) A set containing both sentinel-mapped and non-sentinel members must yield the union of what its members require, not the sentinel alone. Treat the sentinel as a floor contributed by its own member, not a ceiling imposed on the set.
(2) Decide which layer owns the change -- the selector in suite-selection-lib.sh, or validate-artifact.sh's consumption of its output -- and state the reasoning in the implementing commit. Do not fix it in both.
(3) Do not narrow what the selector admits today: a set that resolves to a suite now must resolve to the same suite after the change, and a set whose only members are sentinel-mapped must still return __FULL_SWEEP__.

VERIFY: extend agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/test-run-all-selection.sh (the existing suite for this library -- there is no test-suite-selection-lib.sh) with fixtures pinning (a) a mixed set of one sentinel-mapped bookkeeping path and one narrow real target resolving to the narrow target's suite, (b) an all-sentinel set still returning __FULL_SWEEP__, and (c) an honest two-suite Tier Justification over the mixed set validating with 0 warnings WITHOUT the author dropping the bookkeeping path from "Files to modify". Run from both a source-store and a deployed vantage point.

TERRITORY AND ORDERING. This record declares the same two files as the non-core selection record (suite-selection-lib.sh and tests/test-run-all-selection.sh), which states it holds them alone. That record is already planned and changes the same resolution function, so a dependency edge is FILED rather than relying on a bare exclusion: land it first, then re-derive this defect against the changed selector before editing, since its mapping-walk change may alter which paths are sentinel-mapped at all. Mechanical overlap also exists with the evidence-discipline record and the baseline-relative-criteria record on validate-artifact.sh and tests/test-validate-artifact.sh; subject matter is disjoint, so no edge is filed for those -- re-check at admission time, matching how this backlog treats broad-prefix declarations.

NON-GOALS. No hand-authored file under any deployed .claude/** tree; no redeploy claimed as complete by this task beyond the required deploy-headless.sh run; no broadening of what __FULL_SWEEP__ means for a genuinely repo-wide change; no change to the non-core mapping walk that the other record owns.
=== INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION (appended from a later conclusion-stage channel-b dispatch; everything above this marker is the record as originally filed) ===

A SECOND, INDEPENDENT SIGHTING of this same escalation mode, from a different repository and a different session, confirms the defect and adds one framing worth having. CITATION: task 420, entry iss_1794090946368_48ofpk in specs/420_warn_plan_size_exceeds_cycle_budget/issues.jsonl (class tooling-or-harness-defect, severity minor, plan phase). That entry describes the symptom from the opposite direction: suite_selection_select returns a LARGER set for a multi-path call than the union of per-path calls over the same paths, so a Tier Justification an author composed from PER-PATH invocations under-named its covering suites -- four of them in the observed case, until corrected by hand.

THE TWO DESCRIPTIONS ARE THE SAME DEFECT. The larger multi-path result IS __FULL_SWEEP__, dominating its non-sentinel members exactly as this record's THE DEFECT section states. Measured directly against the source store at the time of this append: `suite_selection_select context/contracts/phase-closure.md scripts/lib/suite-selection-lib.sh` returns `__FULL_SWEEP__`, while `suite_selection_select scripts/lib/suite-selection-lib.sh` alone returns `test-run-all-selection.sh` and `test-validate-artifact.sh`, and `suite_selection_unmapped` over the pair correctly names only the first path. An author who runs the selector per path and discards the sentinel line for the one unmappable path is left naming strictly fewer suites than the multi-path call reports -- which is the under-naming the cited entry recorded.

WHY THE PER-PATH-COMPOSING AUTHOR IS THE MORE DANGEROUS CASE, and the reason this is worth appending rather than filing separately: validate-artifact.sh's Tier Justification check calls `suite_selection_select "${_tj_touched[@]}"` as a single MULTI-PATH call and compares its output against the author's claim. So a per-path-composing author and the checker judging that author disagree by construction, and the checker reports the honest per-path composition as "under-verifies: suite_selection_select additionally returns (...) for this phase's touched paths, not named in the justification". Both the fabrication warning this record already documents and this under-verification warning come from the same set-semantics asymmetry.

IMPLICATION FOR THIS RECORD'S POINT (2) -- which layer owns the fix: this sighting is evidence for the selector layer rather than the consumer layer, since the asymmetry is observable from the library alone with no plan and no validator involved, and any consumer composing per path hits it independently. Treat that as evidence weighing the existing decision, not as the decision itself; this record's point (2) still owns the ruling and still requires it be stated in the implementing commit.

ALSO WORTH PINNING, if cheap: a caller-facing statement of the composition contract. The library's PUBLIC API header already documents the sentinel escalation for `suite_selection_select`, but nothing warns a caller that composing per-path results is NOT equivalent to one multi-path call, which is the mistake both sightings record an author making. A line in the header, or in whatever document instructs an author to run the selector for a Tier Justification, would close the authoring half of this defect alongside the mechanical half.

NO SEPARATE RECORD WAS FILED for the cited entry's selector half, specifically to avoid a duplicate of this record. The same entry's OTHER defect -- validate-artifact.sh's cross-phase ceiling-consistency check misreading a stop-word as a unit noun -- is a disjoint concern in a different code block and is filed separately as fix_ceiling_check_stopword_unit_false_positive, which declares scripts/validate-artifact.sh and tests/test-validate-artifact.sh and so overlaps this record mechanically. That record files no dependency edge to this one, matching the treatment this record already states for the other validate-artifact.sh claimants; if both are admitted together, batch them rather than excluding either.

### 563. Make the extension repo registry usable for deploy enumeration: rule between refusing test-fixture registration and pruning on read
- **Status**: [NOT STARTED]
- **Task Type**: neovim
- **Topic**: extensions
- **Dependencies**: None

**Description**: The cross-repo extension registry at ~/.local/share/nvim/neotex-ai/extension-repo-registry.json is unusable as a deploy-enumeration source. Measured 2026-11-08: 313 entries, of which 311 are /tmp paths and only 2 are real repositories (/home/benjamin/Projects/BimodalLogic and /home/benjamin/Projects/Logos/Theory). The /tmp entries are genuine test-fixture residue -- agent scratchpad trees (/tmp/claude-1000/.../scratchpad/wt435-pre, .../opencode-test/e2e_project) and `mktemp -d` deploy fixtures (/tmp/tmp.00uM2fRkwI/deployed, /tmp/tmp.0k6Zm9RlyP/fixture) -- written by test runs that loaded an extension into a temporary project directory. For comparison, a bounded filesystem scan (`find $HOME -maxdepth 5 -name .claude-extensions.json`) finds 16 repositories carrying a deploy manifest.

Consequence: any consumer that needs to enumerate deployed repos -- a before/after measurement, a fleet-wide sweep, or a control set -- cannot use the registry and must fall back to filesystem enumeration. The immediate consumer already worked around this: the orphan-sweep plan at specs/369_orphan_sweep_for_removed_merge_target_entries/plans/01_orphan-sweep-hook-registrations.md specifies filesystem enumeration rather than the registry as its control-set source. The workaround is in place, so this is not urgent; what remains unfixed is the registry itself.

DECIDE between two candidate shapes rather than assuming one:
(1) Refuse test-fixture registration at write time, so /tmp paths never enter the registry. Addresses the cause; leaves the existing 311 stale entries needing a one-off cleanup. Open sub-question the task must answer: what the refusal predicate actually keys on. A bare /tmp prefix test is the obvious candidate but is not obviously right -- it would also reject a legitimate project a user happens to keep under /tmp, and it would not catch a fixture rooted elsewhere (TMPDIR pointed at a non-/tmp path, or a scratchpad under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR). Consider instead keying on the fixture's own marker, or on an explicit opt-out the test harness sets, and rule on which is defensible.
(2) Prune non-existent and /tmp-anchored entries on read or on a maintenance pass. Self-healing, but keeps writing entries that will later be discarded.
A combination is plausible and should be considered on its merits, not excluded by default.

GROUNDING the task must not re-derive, and must not duplicate: shape (2) is PARTIALLY BUILT ALREADY. `M.prune_unreachable()` exists at lua/neotex/plugins/ai/shared/extensions/repo_registry.lua:182 and removes every registered row whose directory no longer exists on disk. It is wired, but only from one site -- lua/neotex/plugins/ai/claude/commands/picker/init.lua:343 -- inside the interactive `Global Update` picker action, and only when that action has already observed at least one unreachable row (`if #unreachable > 0 then`). So the pruning MECHANISM is not the gap; its TRIGGER is. Nothing prunes on read (`M.read()` at repo_registry.lua:57 returns the file as-is), which is why 311 dead fixture rows have accumulated. Scoping shape (2) as "write prune_unreachable" would be rework; the real shape-(2) question is whether `M.read()`, `M.list()`, or a scheduled maintenance pass should call it, and what that costs on every read.

The registration write path is `M.upsert()` at repo_registry.lua:114, called via `pcall(repo_registry.upsert, project_dir, extension_name)` from lua/neotex/plugins/ai/shared/extensions/init.lua:736 on every successful extension load. `M.upsert` already has one exclusion precedent to follow rather than invent: the HOST-REPO EXCLUSION (`M.is_host_repo`, repo_registry.lua:46), which returns early with success and registers nothing. A shape-(1) fixture exclusion is structurally the same move and should match that shape, including its non-fatal posture -- a registry refusal must never fail an otherwise-successful extension load.

SCOPE NOTE: the registry file itself is runtime state under ~/.local/share/nvim/, not source-controlled content. The fix lands in the Lua code that writes and reads it -- repo_registry.lua, and picker/init.lua if the prune trigger moves -- never in the registry JSON as a checked-in artifact. The one-off cleanup of the 311 existing stale entries is a runtime-state operation, not a repo edit, and should be specified as such (a documented one-shot invocation, not a committed file change).

TASK TYPE RATIONALE: filed as task_type `neovim`, not `meta`. The change request reached this backlog through the agent-system channel, but the implementation site is plain Neovim Lua under lua/neotex/plugins/ai/, so `neovim` routing (neovim-research-agent / planner-agent / neovim-implementation-agent) is the honest routing. No file under .claude/** or agent-system/extensions/** is in scope.

BACKLOG RECONCILIATION, already run (scripts/audit-task-proposals.sh, verdict recorded on this entry's audit_verdict field): the mechanically-corroborated matches are closed tasks that BUILT this registry, not ones that fixed it. Task 45 ("Picker fixes: Global Update extension-repo registry, and honest [Reload All]/[Regenerate] entries", mechanical_class subset, discharging_artifact null) and task 22 created repo_registry.lua and prune_unreachable itself -- task 22's plan records both as completed checklist items. Neither addressed test-fixture pollution or the prune trigger, so this is a follow-up defect on closed work, not a duplicate of it. The 15 duplicate-of-open verdicts are all pure-semantic with mechanical_class "none", no shared paths, and scores 0.42-0.52; per the matcher's own stated posture these are recall-biased shortlist noise, and none concerns the registry.

EVIDENCE CITATION: recorded during task 369's plan phase as issue-log entry iss_1794210505854_rff529 (class: tooling, severity: minor) in specs/369_orphan_sweep_for_removed_merge_target_entries/issues.jsonl.

### 562. conclusion stage drops null-resolution issue-log entries
- **Status**: [NOT STARTED]
- **Task Type**: meta
- **Topic**: agent-system
- **Dependencies**: None

**Description**: Close the contract gap that makes null-resolution issue-log entries invisible to the conclusion stage

THE CONCLUSION STAGE SILENTLY DROPS NULL-RESOLUTION ISSUE-LOG ENTRIES. `context/formats/issue-log.md` declares the `resolution` field optional and nullable (its field table row reads "no (nullable)", closed vocabulary `fixed_inline | worked_around | open`). `context/contracts/conclusion-stage.md`'s "The Filter Predicate" admits an entry into channel classification ONLY when `resolution` is `open` or `worked_around`. An entry written with `resolution: null` is therefore neither closed (`fixed_inline`, which legitimately generates no channel item) nor classified -- it reaches NO channel and is invisible to the user. Both documents are internally consistent; the gap is between them.

VERIFIED LIVE, NOT HYPOTHESIZED. `specs/749_c_bound_half_model_a_presentation_size/issues.jsonl` holds 11 entries, every one with `resolution: null` and `suggested_channel: null`. `bash .claude/scripts/orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh --aggregate --session <sid> --tasks 749` returned `proposals: 0`, `wins: 4`, `unknown_classes: 6`. Of the 11 entries, 7 are `kind: "issue"` and were all dropped: six at `severity: minor` (classes `stale-citation`, `plan-deviation`, `plan-gap`, `plan-gap`, `plan-gap`, `build-failure`) and one at `severity: costly` (class `plan-deviation`). The 4 `kind: "win"` entries surfaced correctly, which confirms the aggregator is behaving exactly as written -- this is a contract mismatch, not an aggregator bug. Re-derive these counts from the live log rather than trusting them; they are a snapshot.

DECIDE AND LAND ONE OF THREE. (a) Make `resolution` REQUIRED at write time in `scripts/issue-record.sh`, so an entry cannot be recorded without one -- closes the hole at the writer, but every existing null-resolution entry across the repo stays invisible. (b) Widen the Filter Predicate to treat null-or-absent `resolution` as `open` -- the conservative reading, since an issue recorded without a resolution is an unresolved one; note this alone would have pushed 7 entries from ONE task into channel classification, so weigh proposal volume before choosing it. (c) Keep both contracts as they are and have the conclusion stage report a separate "unclassifiable (no resolution)" tally beside its unknown-class tally, so the entries are at least visible rather than dropped. Options (a) and (c) are composable; (b) subsumes neither. Whichever is chosen, the two documents MUST end up agreeing in writing -- the acceptance condition for this record is that a reader of either file can predict the other's behavior.

ALSO IN SCOPE. `suggested_channel` was null on all 7 dropped entries too. `conclusion-stage.md`'s "The Hint-Versus-Decision Rule" treats that field as a hint the orchestrator may override visibly, which presumes a hint exists; decide whether a null hint is acceptable or whether the writer should require one, and say so in the same place the `resolution` decision is recorded.

SOURCE-STORE BOUNDARY. All four file_scope paths live in a deployed, regenerated tree -- a hand edit under `.claude/**` is wiped by the next deploy and the edit will appear to succeed while having no lasting effect. Implementation MUST resolve `source_dir` from `<project-root>/.claude-extensions.json` for the owning extension (`core`, whose source store is `/home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/core`) and edit at the mirroring paths there, per `.claude/rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md`, then redeploy via `bash .claude/scripts/deploy-headless.sh` and confirm `RESULT=landed_verify_clean`. The deployed paths are declared in file_scope only so the overlap gate can see the collision surface; they are not the edit target.

DELIVERABLE HYGIENE. The edited files are not under `specs/**`, so the prose must carry no task-number references and no record-versioning language; cite durable anchors (file names, section headings, field names) only.

RELATED RECORDS, FOR ORIENTATION AND NOT AS DEPENDENCY EDGES. The roadmap-generator record covering `roadmap-integration.sh`'s partial-write behavior is the sibling core-extension defect with the same source-store boundary, and the file_scope-declaration-hygiene record covers a different blindness in the same admission machinery. No dependency edge to either -- nothing here blocks on them.

### 561. Record the load-sized bound and the diagnostic-preserving output capture on the bounded-waiter idiom
- **Status**: [NOT STARTED]
- **Task Type**: meta
- **Topic**: agent-system
- **Dependencies**: Task 552

**Description**: Record two conditions the bounded-waiter guidance assumes but never states: that a waiter's bound
must be sized from its writer's measured worst case under CONCURRENT AGENT LOAD rather than its
solo expected runtime, and that a bounded run's output capture must be one that preserves partial
output when the bound fires.

NOTHING IN ANY SCRIPT IS BROKEN AND THIS IS NOT A DATA-REPAIR RECORD. The deliverable is guidance
prose in the core extension's source store plus its index wiring.

=== THE TWO MEASURED FACTS ===

(1) A full `verify-deploy.sh` re-measurement, bounded at `timeout 540` and piped through
`tail -150`, was killed by its own 540s bound before producing ANY output, under concurrent
multi-agent CPU load -- many sibling `verify-deploy.sh` invocations were observed running
concurrently. It completed only on a retry bounded at 900s.

(2) That same killed run yielded ZERO diagnostic signal: the caller could not tell how far it had
got or which gate it died in, because the `tail` pipe emitted nothing. A direct file redirect
preserves partial output across a kill.

=== READ THIS BEFORE WRITING ANY PROSE: THE "RAISE IT TO 900" FRAMING IS WRONG TWICE OVER ===

The obvious reading of fact (1) is "the bound was too small, use 900." Do NOT write that. It is
wrong on two independent, checkable grounds, and both must be reflected in the guidance.

FIRST, 900 DOES NOT FIT. The Bash tool's `timeout` parameter has a documented CEILING of
`600000`ms (600s). An inner `timeout 900` inside a foreground Bash call can therefore never fire:
the harness auto-backgrounds the call at 600s at the latest, which is precisely the failure
`external-process-wait.md` Rule 1 step (2) and `bounded-build-waiter.md`'s canonical-idiom section
both already exist to prevent. A bound above ~540 is not a tuning choice available to the
foreground form at all; it is a statement that the job has left the foreground form's reach.

SECOND, AND MORE IMPORTANTLY, THE BOUND WAS KILLING THE WRONG THING. In the foreground form
(`timeout N cmd`), the bound kills the SUBJECT -- the work is destroyed when the bound fires. In
the detach-plus-waiter form (`cmd >log 2>&1 & pid=$!` then a bounded liveness wait), the bound
ends only the WAITING; the writer runs on and the log survives on disk, so an expired waiter costs
one more bounded call rather than the whole run. The measured incident used the foreground form
for a job that needs the detached one. Under the detached form a 540s waiter expiry is a non-event
and fact (2) cannot arise either, because the writer's output is already going to a file by
redirect.

So the correct resolution of fact (1) is NOT a bigger number. It is that a full `verify-deploy.sh`
run under concurrent batch load is `external-process-wait.md` Rule 1's sub-case 3b -- a job that
cannot fit under the 600s ceiling -- and sub-case 3b is already resolved, in full, by
`bounded-build-waiter.md`'s `### Sizing a Wait Near the Per-Call Ceiling` section: launch once
with a captured PID, then issue a SEQUENCE of separate bounded calls, each gated on liveness and
sized safely under the ceiling, reading the log once liveness ends. THAT SECTION IS ALREADY
CORRECT AND MUST NOT BE REWRITTEN. What is missing is only the sizing INPUT that tells a caller
they are in 3b rather than 3a.

=== THE SIZING INPUT IS THE ACTUAL GAP ===

`bounded-build-waiter.md` Rule 1 currently reads, in part, "Size `N` to the command's expected run
time, within whatever the calling tool allows." A caller reads "expected run time" as the duration
they have observed, which in practice is a solo run on an idle machine. Under a batch
orchestration, concurrent agent load is the NORMAL case rather than the exception, and the
measured spread for this one process crosses the ceiling: comfortably inside 540 solo, above 600
under load. The rule must say that the sizing input is the measured worst case under the
concurrency the job will actually meet, and that when that figure approaches or exceeds the
ceiling the job is 3b and takes the sequence form -- not a larger inner bound.

State this as a property of the sizing INPUT, governed by the EXISTING 3a/3b split. Do NOT
introduce a new numeric threshold of any kind: the 3a/3b split already decides when the sequence
form is warranted, and a second arbiter would contradict it. Any number cited for the tool
`timeout` parameter is `120000`ms (default) or `600000`ms (ceiling).

=== THE OUTPUT-CAPTURE CONDITION, AND THE MEASUREMENT THAT REFUTES THE OBVIOUS PHRASING ===

READ THIS BEFORE WRITING ANY PROSE. It is tempting to state fact (2) as "a pipe buffers, so never
pipe a bounded run." That is measurably WRONG and would be an over-broad prohibition. Measured
directly, a writer emitting 200 lines then sleeping, killed by a 3s bound, with the capture varied:

  (a) `cmd 2>&1 | tail -150 > out`   -- out is 0 bytes, 0 lines. TOTAL LOSS.
  (b) `cmd > out 2>&1`               -- out is 3692 bytes, 200 lines. FULL partial output.
  (c) `cmd 2>&1 | head -150 > out`   -- out is 2742 bytes, 150 lines. Output SURVIVED.
  (d) `cmd 2>&1 | cat > out`         -- out is 3692 bytes, 200 lines. Output SURVIVED IN FULL.

The pipe is not the mechanism. `cat` through a pipe preserved everything and `head -N` preserved
everything it had taken. The mechanism is specific to `tail -N`: it cannot know which lines are
the LAST N until the stream ends, so by its own semantics it emits nothing before EOF, and a kill
before EOF yields nothing at all. The rule to write is therefore a POSITIVE property, not a
blocklist: the capture must be one that writes incrementally and does not require end-of-stream,
for which a direct redirect to a file is the simple guaranteed form. Name `tail -N` as the
concrete violating instance WITH its mechanism, so a reader does not generalize to every pipe and
go looking for pipes to remove elsewhere.

A SECOND, INDEPENDENT DEFECT OF THE PIPE FORM, ALSO MEASURED. The pipeline form destroys the
`exit 124` discrimination that `external-process-wait.md` Rule 1 step (3) depends on. Measured on
the same writer, reproducibly across runs:

  `timeout 3 cmd 2>&1 | tail -150 > out`  -- the caller's `$?` is 143, PIPESTATUS is (124, 143)
  `timeout 3 cmd > out 2>&1`              -- the caller's `$?` is 124

A pipeline's exit status is its LAST command's, so the `124` that step (3) tells the caller to
read as "the bound fired, re-check state rather than reading this as a failure of the command's
subject" is not what `$?` reports; the caller sees 143 and has lost the distinction unless they
reach into `PIPESTATUS[0]`. This is worth stating because it means the pipe form degrades the
bounded-wait contract in two places at once, not just diagnostics.

=== SITING: THREE FILES, AND WHY THE THIRD IS THE ONE THAT NAMES THE GATE ===

Measured by reading the store, the generic-540 prescription the change request describes is NOT in
either pattern file in the form the request implies. Precisely:

  - `context/patterns/bounded-build-waiter.md` Rule 1 owns the local sizing rule ("Size `N` to the
    command's expected run time"). The under-load sizing input belongs HERE. Its
    `## The Canonical Idiom` section owns the `cmd >log 2>&1 & pid=$!` form; the output-capture
    condition belongs HERE, as the stated rationale for a redirect the idiom already uses.
  - `context/patterns/external-process-wait.md` carries the `540`-versus-`600` arithmetic, but its
    `timeout 540` is a `gh run watch` example and the file states explicitly that it covers "the
    case where there is no local writer to probe." A local gate run is not its case. DO NOT edit
    it; its Rule 1 sub-case 3b already points at the bounded-waiter file by name and so inherits
    whatever this record lands. This matches the standing ruling in the sibling record on this
    file family that `external-process-wait.md` carries no restatement.
  - `context/contracts/batch-gate-stage.md` is the file that actually prescribes a bound for THIS
    process. Its `## The Executable Stage Body` step 2 directs the complete `verify-deploy.sh`
    gate set -- run by `scripts/orchestrate-batch-gate.sh`, whose own header states it "Runs the
    complete verify-deploy.sh gate set EXACTLY ONCE for the whole batch" -- to be invoked via "a
    captured PID, a `kill -0` liveness loop, an outer `timeout 540` inside a single Bash tool call
    whose own `timeout` parameter is raised to `600000`."

That last prescription is the sharpest finding in this record and the reason it names a specific
file rather than only amending generic prose. It hard-codes BOTH a 540 bound AND "a single Bash

=== ITEM 1 -- ONE LOW-SPECIFICITY SHARED PATH MUST NOT ALONE PRODUCE duplicate-of-open ===

MEASURED. During a multi-task creation attempt, `audit-task-proposals.sh` returned a
`duplicate-of-open` verdict for a proposal named `oriented_forest_saturation` against open task
869 (`open_modal_invariance_ray_agreement_lifting`) on `mechanical_class: overlap`,
`semantic_score: 0.43`, `shared_paths: ["FormalSystem/Semantics/README.md"]`. Inspection showed
the two are unrelated in content: 869 is open-future/open-past modal invariance along ray
agreement; the proposal was an oriented-forest Saturation lemma. The entire overlap was ONE
shared catch-all README. Disposition at the time: the proposal's declared `file_scope` was
narrowed by hand to drop `FormalSystem/Semantics/README.md`, keeping only
`FormalSystem/Semantics/TaskFrame.lean`, rather than auto-applying a fold or adding a spurious
dependency edge between unrelated records. That manual narrowing is the defect's cost: it
distorts a record's declared scope to satisfy the matcher.

RE-REPRODUCED WHILE THIS RECORD WAS BEING FILED, and this is the strongest available evidence
that the predicate is miscalibrated rather than merely unlucky. An audit of this very proposal
against the live backlog returned `duplicate-of-open` against SIX open records -- 827, 785, 822,
834, plus others -- every one of them with `mechanical_class: "none"` and `shared_paths: []`,
i.e. NO file overlap at all, on semantic scores between 0.41 and 0.48. A verdict named
"duplicate" is being emitted for records that share literally nothing mechanically and that a
reader can confirm in one glance are unrelated. The full audit document is committed as this
record's evidence; re-derive it, do not trust this summary.

WHAT THE SCRIPT ALREADY SAYS ABOUT ITSELF, and why that is not a defence. The script's own
header states plainly that Pass 2 is "a recall-biased, over-inclusive SHORTLIST" and that "THE
SCRIPT NEVER DECIDES DUPLICATION" -- a Pass-2-only verdict is "this script's own best-effort
disposition at its stated threshold", not a certified fact. That posture is correct and must be
PRESERVED: the fix is not to start suppressing records, which the header explicitly forbids. The
problem is the LABEL, not the recall. Emitting the word `duplicate-of-open` for a zero-shared-path,
0.41-semantic-score pair spends the caller's attention and, worse, trains a caller to dismiss the
verdict vocabulary wholesale -- which is precisely how a real duplicate gets filed.

DESIGN QUESTION THE RESEARCH PHASE MUST SETTLE, not a decision this record makes. Candidate
shapes, to be weighed against `context/patterns/backlog-reconciliation.md`'s False-Negative
Posture and D5 (read that document first; it owns the vocabulary and the rationale for every
existing choice):
  (a) require mechanical corroboration -- a non-`none`, non-`scope-blind` mechanical_class --
      before the `duplicate-of-open` label may be used, demoting the uncorroborated cases to a
      weaker existing verdict (`overlaps-open`) or to a new shortlist-only label;
  (b) weight a shared path by its specificity, so a catch-all (`README.md`, `index.json`,
      `manifest.json`, a directory-level entry) counts for less than a leaf source file, with
      a single low-specificity path alone insufficient for `duplicate-of-open`;
  (c) raise the semantic threshold for the uncorroborated case only, leaving the corroborated
      case where it is.
Whichever is chosen, the chosen rule belongs in `backlog-reconciliation.md` alongside the
vocabulary it constrains, and gets a regression case in
`scripts/tests/test-audit-task-proposals.sh`. NO SUPPRESSION: every corpus record must still
appear in the output with SOME verdict, per the script's standing no-suppression guarantee.

=== ITEM 2 -- COMPONENT 7 UNDER AN /orchestrate DISPATCH ===

MEASURED CONTRACT AMBIGUITY, resolved once by hand and not written down. The Multi-Task Creation
Standard's Component 7 requires foreground user confirmation before tasks are filed. Inside an
`/orchestrate` dispatch there is no foreground user to confirm, and the dispatched task's own
description can itself pre-authorize the filing (the observed wording: "file the implementation
as its own task"). The two requirements collide, and the standard is silent on the collision.

HOW IT WAS RESOLVED IN PRACTICE, which is the candidate the standard should either adopt or
explicitly reject: the dispatch treated the task description's own pre-authorization as
standing in for the Component 7 prompt, kept the full Component 4b audit evidence intact, and
RENDERED the Component 7 confirmation table into the task summary as a durable record instead
of prompting with it. The deviation was stated as an assumption in the plan's Risks table rather
than applied silently.

WHAT THIS RECORD OWES. State the resolution in
`docs/reference/standards/multi-task-creation-standard.md`'s Component 7 section: who may
pre-authorize, what artifact the confirmation table must be written into when it is not
prompted, and -- the part the hand-resolution did not settle -- whether a pre-authorization must
be explicit in the dispatched task's description or whether the `/orchestrate` context alone
suffices. Note that `meta-builder-agent` cannot call `AskUserQuestion` at all (it is withheld
from dispatched subagents), so Component 7 is ALREADY relocated upstream to `skill-meta`'s
pre-delegation stage for the `/meta` path; the clause must be consistent with that existing
relocation rather than contradict it.

**Description**: Document the convention that a task description must ask an autonomous dispatch for a PROPOSAL PACKET, never for task FILING, because filing requires a foreground user confirmation no dispatched agent can perform.

THE DEFECT, STATED AS AN UNSATISFIABLE INSTRUCTION. A task description phrased as "let the conclusion stage file what survives" -- or any equivalent wording that directs an autonomous research/plan/implement dispatch to file follow-up tasks -- cannot be honored by the agent that receives it. `docs/reference/standards/multi-task-creation-standard.md`'s Component 7 makes user confirmation mandatory and foreground-only, and `AskUserQuestion` is categorically withheld from every dispatched subagent, so the dispatch has no route to the confirmation the standard requires. The instruction is not merely awkward; it is impossible to execute as written.

VERBATIM EVIDENCE, QUOTED FROM THE ORIGINATING ISSUE-LOG ENTRY AND NOT PARAPHRASED: "The dispatch defers task filing to 'the conclusion stage', but the Multi-Task Creation Standard's Component 7 makes user confirmation mandatory and foreground-only, so no autonomous implement dispatch can file the recommended tasks. The plan resolves this by having the implement phase render a reconciled proposal packet plus issues.jsonl follow_up_task entries instead of filing, leaving the Component 7 decision with the user."

THE COST IS REDISCOVERY, NOT FAILURE. Nothing was lost on the originating run: the dispatch noticed the conflict, invented a workaround (render a reconciled proposal packet plus `issues.jsonl` `follow_up_task` entries instead of filing), and left the Component 7 decision with the user. That is the correct behaviour. The defect is that every dispatch handed such an instruction must independently rediscover the same conflict and independently reinvent the same workaround, spending reasoning tokens on a question the system has already answered -- and a dispatch that does NOT notice will either stall at an unreachable confirmation or file tasks without the confirmation the standard requires. The originating entry's `severity: minor` and `resolution: worked_around` are both correct and should not be inflated.

THE CAPABILITY IS NOT MISSING -- ONLY THE PHRASING CONVENTION IS. Do not scope this as "add a way for dispatches to file tasks". The orchestration conclusion stage (`context/contracts/conclusion-stage.md`, Move 5) ALREADY carries the Component 7 gate: its channel (c), "follow-up tasks as children", is executed at the orchestrate-lead level where `AskUserQuestion` is reachable, and its Step 4b channel already routes agent-system change requests through a confirmed dispatch to the task-creating agent. Read "The Exactly-One-Channel Rule", "The Hint-Versus-Decision Rule", and Step 4c before writing anything. The hand-off mechanism works. What is undocumented is how a task description should PHRASE its hand-off to that mechanism: the description must ask the dispatch to produce the evidence the lead will confirm (a proposal packet, `issues.jsonl` entries with `suggested_channel`), never to perform the filing itself.

DIAGNOSE THE SITING BEFORE COMMITTING TO A REMEDY -- THIS IS DELIBERATELY NOT PRE-DECIDED. Three candidate sites, to be evaluated with evidence rather than ranked here:
  (a) The task-authoring standard. A convention stated once in `docs/reference/standards/multi-task-creation-standard.md`, adjacent to Component 7's own Foreground Requirement, saying that a task description MUST NOT instruct a dispatch to file tasks and MUST instead request a proposal packet. Weigh: that document governs the CREATION surfaces (`/task`, `/meta`, `/spawn`, the conclusion stage), so a reader composing a task description may not consult it.
  (b) The conclusion-stage contract. A statement in `context/contracts/conclusion-stage.md` that the stage consumes proposal packets and `issues.jsonl` entries, and that a task description naming this stage as the filer is malformed. Weigh: this is where the reader who wrote the offending phrasing was already looking, but the stage is only one of several consumers of such a hand-off.
  (c) The dispatch-composition path. A note emitted or embedded where a dispatch body is assembled (`scripts/orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh` and the aux/unwind variants), telling the receiving agent that filing is out of reach and a packet is wanted. Weigh: this reaches the agent at the moment of need and needs no reader discipline, but it treats a symptom of a badly-phrased description rather than preventing the phrasing.
A composition of (a) with one of (b)/(c) is acceptable. Whatever is chosen, state the rejected options on their own merits, with the reason recorded.

WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS WORK WORTHLESS. A second, differently-worded convention. If the proposal-packet shape is already described anywhere -- check the follow-up/skeleton-plan mechanism that `conclusion-stage.md`'s "The Coexistence Boundary With the Skeleton-Plan Follow-Up Mechanism" section names, and the `follow_up_task` vocabulary in `context/formats/issue-log.md` -- then the deliverable is a POINTER to that existing shape plus the prohibition, not a fresh specification of a packet format. Establish what already exists before writing new prose.

NON-GOALS. No change to Component 7's foreground requirement or to any confirmation gate -- the requirement is correct and is the reason this convention is needed. No new capability for dispatched agents to file tasks, and no relaxation of the `AskUserQuestion` withholding. No change to the conclusion stage's channel routing, filter predicate, or exactly-one-channel rule. No retroactive rewriting of existing task descriptions that carry the offending phrasing; if a sweep for them is wanted, it is its own record.

ACCEPTANCE. (1) The convention is stated once, at a single chosen site, with pointers from the others rather than restatement. (2) It names the concrete forbidden shape (a description instructing a dispatch to file tasks) and the concrete required shape (a description requesting a proposal packet plus issue-log entries, with the filing decision left to a foreground surface). (3) It names WHY -- Component 7's foreground requirement and the subagent tool withholding -- so a future reader can re-derive the rule instead of taking it on faith. (4) Redeploy via `bash .claude/scripts/deploy-headless.sh` and confirm `RESULT=landed_verify_clean`.

SOURCE-STORE BOUNDARY -- BINDING. `.claude/**` in this repository is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from a source store; a hand edit there is silently wiped by the next regeneration and will appear to succeed while having no lasting effect. The owning extension is `core`. Resolve its source store with `jq -r '.extensions.core.source_dir' .claude-extensions.json` -- note `source_dir` is PER-EXTENSION, so a top-level `jq -r '.source_dir'` returns `null`, which must NOT be read as the key being absent; when the per-extension lookup yields nothing, the store is `/home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/core`. Edit at the paths mirroring the deployed ones under that store, per `.claude/rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md`, then redeploy. Never hand-author under `.claude/**`.

DELIVERABLE HYGIENE. Every edited file lies outside `specs/**`, so its prose must carry no task-number references (`.claude/rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md`) and no record-versioning language (`.claude/rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md`). Cite durable anchors only: file names, section headings, component names ("Component 7"), field names (`suggested_channel`, `follow_up_task`), and tool names (`AskUserQuestion`). The originating task number and the issue entry_id below belong in this description only, never in deliverable prose.

PROVENANCE AND CITATION. Raised by /orchestrate's conclusion stage and approved at the orchestrate-lead level as an agent-system change request, session `sess_1793900475_c93eff`. The originating issue-log entry, cited verbatim for audit against its evidence: {task 872, entry_id iss_1793901844876_M9V2B8}, in `specs/872_open_language_transfer_ledger/issues.jsonl` -- `class: design-record defect or ambiguity`, `severity: minor`, `phase: plan`, `dispatch_seq: 2`, `resolution: worked_around`, `suggested_channel: follow_up_task`, `evidence_path: .claude/docs/reference/standards/multi-task-creation-standard.md`. Read that entry verbatim before composing anything. BACKLOG-RECONCILIATION RULING, RECORDED HONESTLY: `scripts/audit-task-proposals.sh` returned only pure-semantic `duplicate-of-open` verdicts for this proposal, every one with `mechanical_class: none` and the highest at `semantic_score: 0.525` -- below any corroboration. The three nearest open records were read and each addresses a different mechanism: one closes the conclusion stage's filter predicate against `resolution: null` entries, one closes plan-authoring self-consistency gaps, and one concerns an inherited error count on a stall re-prompt. None governs how a task description phrases its hand-off to a foreground confirmation. The proposal is ruled genuinely new on that reading, not on the matcher's recall-biased output.
