### 556. Fix validate-handoff.sh crash-as-false-negative and settle the canonical blockers shape
- **Status**: [NOT STARTED]
- **Task Type**: meta
- **Topic**: agent-system
- **Dependencies**: None

**Description**: META TASK. Fix a validator that reports a well-formed handoff as invalid, and settle the
canonical `blockers` shape that three different authorities currently disagree about.

=== MEASURED SYMPTOM, RE-DERIVABLE ===

During cycle 2 postflight of the ladder-realization work, `orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh` ran
`validate-handoff.sh` against that task's `.orchestrator-handoff.json`. The validator printed
eleven consecutive `[PASS]` lines and not one `[FAIL]`, then postflight emitted:
  ERROR: HANDOFF VALIDATION FAILED - <file> fails validate-handoff.sh's required-field checks
Reproduce (read-only):
  bash .claude/scripts/validate-handoff.sh specs/761_ladder_realization_theorem/.orchestrator-handoff.json; echo "EXIT=$?"
Observed: EXIT=5, and the output STOPS after "Blockers array present with 3 entry(s)" - the
"All blockers have required fields" line, the Validation Summary block, and the final verdict
line are all absent. The validator never reaches its own summary.

=== ROOT CAUSE, PINNED - NOT A HYPOTHESIS ===

`validate-handoff.sh` sets `set -euo pipefail`. Its Check 7 block, having confirmed a non-empty
`blockers` array, loops over the entries probing each as an OBJECT:
  has_phase=$(jq -r ".blockers[$i].phase // \"__MISSING__\"" "$HANDOFF_FILE" 2>/dev/null)
In the observed handoff the `blockers` entries are STRINGS, not objects. Indexing a string with
`.phase` is a jq runtime error ("Cannot index string with ..."), jq exits 5, `2>/dev/null`
discards the message, and under `set -e` the failed command substitution terminates the script
immediately with that exit 5. Confirm the per-entry failure directly:
  jq -r '.blockers[0].phase' specs/761_ladder_realization_theorem/.orchestrator-handoff.json; echo "EXIT=$?"
Note that 5 is not a documented exit code: the script's own header documents only 0 (valid),
1 (invalid) and 3 (file not found). The script therefore has an undocumented crash exit that is
indistinguishable, to any caller testing `-ne 0`, from a legitimate validation failure.

=== WHY THE CONSEQUENCE IS WORSE THAN A WRONG MESSAGE ===

The postflight call site treats any non-zero exit as a required-field failure, then tries to name
the failing fields by parsing `^\[FAIL\]` lines out of the captured output. A crash produces no
FAIL lines, so that parse yields an empty list and the `--extra-detail-json` flag is omitted by
the call site's own never-guess rule. The result is a HANDOFF_VALIDATION_FAILED system defect
raised against a handoff that is in fact well-formed, carrying no evidence of what failed,
because nothing did. A defect channel that reports healthy inputs as defective erodes trust in
every other entry it carries; this one firing is enough to warrant the fix.

=== THE REAL DISAGREEMENT: WHAT SHAPE IS `blockers`? ===

Settle this FIRST; it decides which side of the fix is the non-conforming one. Three authorities
disagree, measured:
  (a) `context/schemas/orchestrator-handoff-schema.json` - `blockers.items` is `type: "object"`
      with `required: ["phase", "target"]`, plus optional `verbatim_goal`, `what_was_tried`,
      `why_it_failed`. Its own description calls this "Canonical wrap-up/hard-mode blocker shape".
  (b) `extensions/lean/agents/lean-implementation-hard-agent.md` - instructs, in prose: "On
      `partial` or `blocked`: populate `blockers` with verbatim goal text from plan checklist."
      Followed literally, that yields an array of STRINGS, which is what the live handoff holds.
  (c) `validate-handoff.sh` Check 7 - probes `.phase`/`.target` unguarded, i.e. assumes (a) and
      crashes rather than failing on (b).
So the writer's instruction and the schema contradict each other, and the validator cannot survive
the contradiction. Do not resolve this by guarding the validator alone: that would leave a writer
producing data its own schema rejects, silently. Decide which shape is canonical, then conform the
other two sides to it, and say in the plan which authority was chosen and why.

A fourth data point to weigh, because it cuts against (b): the open record
`postflight_detail_free_blocking_partial_issue_entry` (task 770) asserts as measured fact that
"the live returns carry `{phase, target, verbatim_goal, what_was_tried, why_it_failed}`" and that
jq's `join` on them errors. Both that record and this one observed a jq exit 5 on `blockers`, from
OPPOSITE shape assumptions - which means the shape varies across writers or across time. Establish
the actual distribution before ruling; a ruling that explains only one of the two observations is
incomplete. Check the object-shaped and string-shaped producers separately rather than assuming one
global shape.

=== STRUCTURAL HARDENING, IN SCOPE ===

Independently of the shape ruling: an unguarded `jq` under `set -euo pipefail` with `2>/dev/null`
converts any data-shape surprise into a silent, undocumented, non-zero exit with no diagnostic.
Make the validator detect a shape it cannot probe and report it as a real `[FAIL]` line with a
documented exit code, so the summary block is always reached and callers can distinguish
"invalid handoff" from "validator crashed". Removing or redirecting the error-swallowing
`2>/dev/null` on these probes is in scope and is the reason this was invisible.

=== TERRITORY - DO NOT TAKE THESE FILES ===

`orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh` is claimed by three open records (tasks 770, 823 and 842) and
`system-defect-record.sh` by task 842. This record deliberately declares NEITHER, and confines
itself to the validator, the schema and the lean hard agent's instruction. If the fix turns out to
require changing how the call site interprets the validator's exit status - a reasonable outcome,
since distinguishing crash from failure is only useful if the caller acts on it - add a dependency
edge with `update-task-status.sh --depends-on-add` rather than editing a file another record owns.
Recommended sequencing to raise at plan time: this record's shape ruling is load-bearing for task
770, whose fix renders blocker entries into prose on the assumption they are objects. Settle the
shape here first, or fold the two together deliberately.

=== EDIT TARGET, BINDING ===

Per `rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md` this repository's `.claude/` tree is a gitignored,
disposable deploy artifact regenerated from a source store; a file hand-authored under `.claude/**`
is silently wiped by the next regeneration and the edit will appear to succeed while having no
lasting effect. Edit under the source store at the mirroring path. Re-derive it rather than
trusting this note - `source_dir` lives PER EXTENSION, not at top level:
  jq -r '.extensions.core.source_dir' .claude-extensions.json
  jq -r '.extensions.lean.source_dir' .claude-extensions.json
A top-level `jq -r '.source_dir'` returns null; that is the key being nested, not absent. Reading
of this record's creation: `/home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/{core,lean}`.
After editing, redeploy with `bash .claude/scripts/deploy-headless.sh` and confirm the result is
a clean verify. Stage narrowly: explicit file lists only, never a directory or glob pathspec.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===

- The reproduction command above exits 0 with the Validation Summary block present, OR exits with
  a documented code after printing at least one `[FAIL]` line naming the real problem. A silent
  non-zero with only PASS lines is the defect and must not survive.
- Extend the validator's test coverage (do not replace existing cases) with one string-shaped
  `blockers` fixture and one object-shaped fixture, and show the string-shaped case fails against
  the unmodified script.
- The shape ruling is recorded in the plan with its chosen authority, and whichever of the schema
  or the lean hard agent instruction is non-conforming is actually amended - not left to drift.
- The validator's header exit-code list matches its real exit paths.

=== DELIVERABLE HYGIENE ===

Every edited file is outside `specs/**`, so its prose must carry no task-number references
(`rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md`) and no record-versioning language
(`rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md`). Cite durable anchors - file names, function
names, check names, field names, flag names - only.

=== PROVENANCE ===

Observed live in session `sess_1793823065_4dcf25`, cycle 2 of task 761, and approved at the
orchestrate-lead level as an agent-system change request. The run's detected-defect entry carries
defect_class HANDOFF_VALIDATION_FAILED, detecting_site
`skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md:cycle-postflight-handoff-validation`. The mathematical work of the
originating task closed green (full `lake build` exit 0, sorry 0, five repo gates passing); this
is a fault in the agent system, not in that work.


=== CANDIDATE DUPLICATE, NOT YET RULED (2026-11-04) ===

The source-store repository's open record #472 handoff_validator_crash_and_defect_record_gap
addresses the same validate-handoff.sh crash as this record. #472 is 15,791 characters against this
record's 8,752 and carries a second half this record does not (the defect recorder refusing every
consumer-repo attribution). This record's own promise to settle the canonical blockers shape may or
may not fall inside #472's scope, and neither record cites an entry_id, so there is no provenance
shortcut. RULING THIS PAIR REQUIRES READING BOTH IN FULL -- it was deliberately left undecided
rather than guessed from the titles. The identifier #472 is a number in THAT repository's task space
and does not resolve here.

- **Status**: [NOT STARTED]

**Description**: MEASURED during task 846's Phase 5. `run-all.sh` with no filter reported 26 failing suites of 156 (130 passed). Citations, from task 846's `issues.jsonl`: iss_1793736739875_sDC3Vt, iss_1793740991529_beV238.

Two of the 26 are the repo's own `known-failures.txt` baseline (`.claude/scripts/tests/known-failures.txt`) and are expected. The remaining 24 all trace to ONE cause: this repository has never had a local `agent-system/extensions` directory, its source store being external via `.claude-extensions.json`. That cause was confirmed directly on 7 of the 24: `test-askuserquestion-rehome.sh`, `test-deploy-propagation.sh`, `test-gate-cache-lib.sh`, `test-orchestrate-build-aux-dispatch.sh`, `test-routing-resolution.sh`, `test-update-task-status.sh`, `test-lint-dead-command-recommendations.sh`. WHY IT MATTERS. A permanently-red sweep masks real findings: a genuinely new failure does not change the exit code and is invisible to anyone reading only the exit status. This is the same pathology the existing record `state_counter_archive_numbering_reconciliation` (see `specs/821_state_counter_archive_numbering_reconciliation/`) documented for `validate-state.sh`. (2) The exit code again discriminates a new failure from the standing baseline. (3) No suite is silenced without a recorded reason.

### 554. file_scope containment drops external source-store paths from phase commits
- **Effort**: medium
- **Status**: [NOT STARTED]
- **Task Type**: meta
- **Topic**: agent-system
- **Dependencies**: None

**Description**: OBSERVED 13 times during task 846's implementation. Every `agent-system/extensions/core/**` path was dropped from its phase-commit pathspec by `git-commit-phase.sh`, each reported with the message text `not contained in this task's declared file_scope` (git-commit-phase.sh, the `--what-happened` string at the excursion-report call site). Citations, all from task 846's `issues.jsonl`: iss_1793736794251_k7Q3J8, iss_1793736794311_yUp8Vp, iss_1793737815724_0ZfGnJ, iss_1793737815788_QHk1wn, iss_1793737815847_SJ3yxu, iss_1793737815907_UKDkzX, iss_1793737815965_izbdkL, iss_1793737816029_P1dXET, iss_1793737816087_3YZSsX, iss_1793738678082_9E2Jin, iss_1793738678146_o1Q504, iss_1793741189717_sYrKgg, iss_1793741189826_eDqokf.

TWO COMPOUNDING CAUSES. The task must address both or state explicitly why not.

(1) This repository's source store is EXTERNAL. `jq -r '.extensions.core.source_dir' .claude-extensions.json` resolves to `/home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/core` -- a different git repository. A path there is not under this repo's root at all, so a containment check against this repo's `file_scope` cannot match it, and a commit in this repo could not carry it even if the check passed. Independently confirmed: `agent-system/` does not exist in this repository at all, so even the plain `agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/...` entries present in task 846's `file_scope` match nothing locally.

(2) The declared `file_scope` carried LITERAL, UNEXPANDED `$SD/...` entries. ### 553. Name the typst-sync gate as the cause when git-commit-scoped.sh reports a refused commit
- **Effort**: low
- **Status**: [NOT STARTED]
- **Task Type**: meta
- **Topic**: agent-system
- **Dependencies**: Task 548

**Description**: META TASK. ONE defect, ONE record: when `git-commit-scoped.sh`'s commit attempt is refused by
this repository's typst-sync pre-commit gate, the script's own caller-facing verdict misnames the
cause as the V8 silent-staging-drop defect and calls the refusal "non-blocking", naming neither
the gate that refused nor the remedy that clears it. The deliverable is the DIAGNOSTIC MESSAGE
ONLY.

EDIT TARGET, binding. Per `rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md` this repository's `.claude/`
tree is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from a source store; a hand-authored
file landing under `.claude/**` is silently wiped by the next regeneration -- the edit appears to
succeed and has no lasting effect. Make every edit under the source store at the path mirroring
the deployed `.claude/scripts/git-commit-scoped.sh`. RE-DERIVE the store rather than trusting
this note, but know what re-derivation currently yields: `source_dir` lives PER-EXTENSION at
`.extensions.<name>.source_dir` in `<project-root>/.claude-extensions.json`, not as a top-level
key. A top-level `jq -r '.source_dir'` returns null and must NOT be read as the key being
absent. Re-derive with:

  jq -r '.extensions.core.source_dir' .claude-extensions.json

which currently yields `/home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/core`, so the edit
target is `agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/git-commit-scoped.sh`. The owning extension is
`core`, not `typst` and not `lean`: the file to change is the commit wrapper, not the gate. If
`source_dir` is absent or its path does not exist when this task runs, record that as an
observation of its own rather than silently hand-authoring under `.claude/**`.

=== THE DEFECT AS OBSERVED ===

MEASURED {task 838, entry_id iss_1793728724405_1fBgOG} (class `gate collision`, severity
`costly`, resolution open). A commit touching `FormalSystem/**/*.lean` is refused by the
typst-sync pre-commit gate unless the same commit also carries a regenerated
`typst/generated/status.typ`, whose theorem and line counts are derived from the Lean tree.
`git-commit-scoped.sh` surfaced this as a "PARTIAL commit" report rather than naming the gate as
the cause.

COST, which is why this is filed rather than absorbed. It recurred at EVERY phase of that
implementation run, and each recurrence cost a diagnosis cycle -- the operator had to re-derive
the same cause from the same misleading text repeatedly. One recurrence additionally provoked a
reproduction probe that committed `README.md` under the placeholder message `x` (commit
`947dd9e8d`); the amend that would have folded it into the phase commit was refused by the
history-rewrite guard because a concurrent writer was live, so that commit remains in history.
That stray commit is a consequence of the misdiagnosis, not a separate defect, and it is NOT in
scope here: do not attempt to rewrite history to remove it.

THE REMEDY THAT ACTUALLY WORKED, each time, and the text the new message must carry:

  bash scripts/typst-sync-check.sh --fix
  # then add typst/generated/status.typ to the commit pathspec

=== MECHANISM -- VERIFIED BY SOURCE READING, NOT YET REPRODUCED END-TO-END ===

The following is a reading of the deployed script at the time this record was written. Confirm it
against the source store before acting, and confirm the end-to-end shape by actually driving a
refusal; the claims below are code-path reasoning plus the measured symptom, not a reproduction.

(1) `commit_output=$(git commit -m "$full_message" -- "${pathspecs[@]}" 2>&1)` captures the
    hook's stderr, and `echo "$commit_output"` later emits it on STDOUT. The gate's own text is
    therefore present but buried mid-stream, below the script's own authoritative-sounding
    stderr lines.

(2) The V8 post-commit integrity gate runs UNCONDITIONALLY, regardless of `commit_exit` -- its
    own header comment says so. When the hook refuses, no commit is created, so every
    V8-snapshotted path compares as `absent from HEAD` (or as differing content), V8's mismatch
    array is non-empty, and it prints on stderr: "ERROR: git-commit-scoped.sh detected a PARTIAL
    commit -- one or more named positive pathspecs did not land in HEAD as intended (Verified
    Finding V8). This is the silent-staging-drop defect: ...". That attribution is WRONG for this
    shape. Nothing was silently dropped; a gate refused the whole commit.

(3) `if [ "$commit_exit" -ne 0 ]; then echo "NOTE: Nothing to commit or git commit failed
    (non-blocking)" >&2; fi` then characterizes a HARD gate refusal as non-blocking, which
    invites exactly the wrong response -- proceeding as though nothing is owed.

(4) THE EXIT CODE IS ALREADY CORRECT AND MUST NOT CHANGE. V8's dedicated `exit 5` is guarded by
    `[ "$commit_exit" -eq 0 ]`, so it does NOT fire on a refusal; the script falls through to
    `exit "$commit_exit"`, which is git's own nonzero code. The defect is PURELY TEXTUAL. A fix
    that alters exit codes has exceeded its scope.

WHERE THE GATE LIVES, as durable anchors the new message may name. `core.hooksPath` is
`.githooks`, so the gate is `.githooks/pre-commit`; it invokes
`scripts/typst-sync-check.sh --counts-only`, fires only when the staged set touches a `.lean`
path, and is blocking rather than auto-regenerating. Its own text already names the remedy
(`lake build && bash scripts/typst-sync-check.sh --fix && git add typst/generated/status.typ`).
The gate is NOT broken and must not be edited by this task -- the hook's diagnosis is correct; it
is the wrapper's verdict on top of it that is wrong.

=== THE DESIGN QUESTION TO SETTLE, NOT A PARSER TO PATCH ===

`git-commit-scoped.sh` is deployed into repositories that do not have a typst gate, so the fix
must NOT hard-code one repository's hook. Research must settle which of these the change is, and
say why:

  (a) Detect the refusal class generically -- a nonzero `commit_exit` whose `commit_output`
      indicates a pre-commit hook refusal rather than an empty diff -- and reframe BOTH the V8
      ERROR and the "non-blocking" NOTE for that shape, re-emitting the hook's own captured text
      as the authoritative cause instead of burying it. This generalizes to every hook in every
      deploy and names no repository-specific path in the script.
  (b) Additionally pattern-match the typst-sync gate specifically to name `--fix` and the
      `status.typ` pathspec in the wrapper's own words.

(a) is the structurally sound half and is likely sufficient on its own, since the hook already
prints the remedy and (a) promotes that text rather than paraphrasing it. Prefer (a); adopt (b)
only if research shows the hook's text does not in fact reach the caller, and if it does, keep
any repository-specific knowledge out of the script body. The minimum acceptable outcome is that
a reader of the script's output can tell a gate refusal from a staging drop WITHOUT re-reading
the script.

=== TERRITORY -- WHY THIS DEPENDS ON THE CONTINGENCY/CONTAINMENT RECORD ===

Open record #839 (`plan_contingency_file_scope_and_containment_drop`, not_started) already claims
`agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/git-commit-scoped.sh` AND
`agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/test-git-commit-scoped.sh` in its `file_scope` --
both of this record's files. The two changes are INDEPENDENT in substance: #839 settles the V10
containment guard and the `plan-file-scope-harvest.sh` contract, which is a different code path
from the post-commit reporting block changed here. Neither subsumes the other and neither should
be closed as a duplicate of the other.

They are nonetheless the same file with no mechanism to serialize them, which `.claude/CLAUDE.md`'s
batching guardrail names as a reason to sequence rather than exclude. The edge runs #839 -> this
record, with #839 first, because #839 is the structural change that may itself move the reporting
block this record edits, and because #839 must settle a design question before its own code lands.
Applying the smaller message change on top of the settled structure is strictly cheaper than the
reverse. If #839 is abandoned or descoped away from `git-commit-scoped.sh`, this record becomes
independent and the edge may be dropped.

=== SCOPE BOUNDARY -- THREE THINGS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED ===

(1) THE PLAN-AUTHORING HALF IS ALREADY OWNED ELSEWHERE. Open record #785
    (`lean_plan_gate_collision_authoring_guidance`, not_started) owns the gate-collision facts a
    Lean implementation plan must anticipate BEFORE a criterion is written -- including this
    exact typst-sync surface, its `--fix` remedy, and the pre-commit-versus-later-verification
    asymmetry. Its `file_scope` is entirely within the lean extension and does not overlap this
    record. DO NOT write plan-authoring guidance here and DO NOT duplicate #785. It is named as
    related context only: a reader who wants "how should a plan have avoided this" goes there,
    while this record answers only "what should the script have said when it happened".

(2) The stray `947dd9e8d` commit and the history-rewrite guard refusal described above are
    consequences, not deliverables. No history rewrite.

(3) Two further findings from the same run were considered for this channel and DELIBERATELY
    EXCLUDED by the user's choice. They are NOT in scope and no task is to be created for them:
    the Scope-Hypothesis inventory-consumer miscount, and the non-importable prototype file under
    `specs/**`.

=== DELIVERABLE HYGIENE ===

Every edited file lies outside `specs/**`, so its contents -- including any new message string --
must carry no task-number references (`.claude/rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md`) and

=== ACCEPTANCE ===

THIS IS NOT A GUIDANCE GAP. `extensions/core/context/patterns/bounded-build-waiter.md` already
states every rule the strand broke: Rule 1 (wrap the wait in `timeout N` so the waiter cannot
outlive its writer), Rule 3 (a dead writer ends the wait immediately -- treat a missing sentinel as
"the writer died", never as "keep waiting"), Rule 4 (one waiter per log; a second would-be waiter
attaches or fails loudly and "must never silently stop and hand the turn back"), and its "Shape
Taxonomy" section, whose shape 1 prohibits `Bash(run_in_background: true)` and an armed `Monitor`
outright for agent-chosen local-gate backgrounding. The observed strand is a VIOLATION of rules
that already exist in full. The deliverable is therefore mechanical coverage, not more prose.

THE GAP, measured by reading the hook. `extensions/core/hooks/validate-bounded-waiter.sh` enforces
Rule 2 ONLY -- its own header says so, naming Rule 2's prohibition on `ps | grep`, `pgrep -f` and
any process-name-matching test -- and it does so by pattern-matching the raw command STRING,
deliberately without parsing shell structure. Nothing mechanically catches:
  - a wait with no outer `timeout` (Rule 1);
  - a wait with no `kill -0` liveness check backing it (Rule 3);
  - a `Bash(run_in_background: true)` or armed-`Monitor` wait (shape 1's outright prohibition).
Rule 2 has a blocking gate. The rules the strand actually broke have none.

WHAT TO DECIDE AND RECORD. Which of those shapes is detectable from the command string alone at
the hook's existing fidelity, and which is not. A shape that is NOT detectable must be recorded as
not-detectable WITH THE REASON -- never approximated by a lint that fires on correct code, since
this hook blocks. Note in particular that detecting the ABSENCE of a liveness check is a different
problem from detecting a textual pattern's presence, and that the `run_in_background` and `Monitor`
shapes are tool-call parameters rather than command text, so they may not be visible to a
command-string hook at all; if they are not, name the surface that could see them instead of
forcing them into this one.

DO NOT REOPEN A SETTLED DECISION WITHOUT ENGAGING IT. The hook's own header already REJECTS a
shared pattern library for this file, recording the `validate-no-task-references.sh` /
`scripts/lib/task-reference-patterns.sh` split as the established precedent and explaining why it
does not apply here. If this record's fix needs that split after all, address the recorded
reasoning directly rather than silently adopting the rejected shape.

guardrail's rule for an unordered overlap is to add the edge and run as a sequence. That task's

ITEM 2's question (a) -- "the recording path for this class is broken (the check fires, but the
`system-defect-record.sh` call is absent, mis-ordered, or swallowed)" -- is now answered
AFFIRMATIVELY for a DIFFERENT defect class, with a concrete mechanism that very likely

recording failed (non-fatal)". No durable record reached `specs/events.jsonl`.

MECHANISM, read off the code. In `orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh` the HANDOFF_VALIDATION_FAILED
call to `system-defect-record.sh` passes `--dispatched-agent "$agent_name"` but NOT
`--attributed-path`. Compare the three sibling call sites in the SAME script -- the return-meta
partial-progress site, the stray-handoff site and the stale-handoff site -- each of which passes
`--attributed-path "$attributed_path"`. `system-defect-record.sh` requires at least one of the
two and, per its own header, REFUSES (exit 3, "Signal B attribution unresolvable") when the
supplied value does not resolve to a path under `agent-system/extensions/**`. Its resolver for
`--dispatched-agent` globs `"$PROJECT_ROOT"/agent-system/extensions/*/agents/<agent>.md`. In a
deploy-target repository such as this one there is NO `agent-system/` tree at the project root
(confirm: `ls -d agent-system` is empty; the source store lives at
`/home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system`), so `--dispatched-agent` alone can never resolve
here and the recorder refuses every time. The `2>/dev/null` on the call discards the refusal
message, leaving only the non-fatal note.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS RECORD'S OWN METHOD. The pattern to hunt is a call site that omits
`--attributed-path` and relies on `--dispatched-agent` alone; audit EVERY
`system-defect-record.sh` call site in the script for that omission rather than fixing the one
class that happened to be observed. The masking `2>/dev/null` is why this was invisible and is
worth removing or redirecting on these calls. This also means any recurrence count taken from
`specs/events.jsonl` UNDERSTATES reality for precisely those classes whose call sites omit
`--attributed-path` -- which sharpens this record's own stated worry that item 1's sample cannot
be trusted until item 2 is fixed.

RELATED, NO EDGE: the validator whose false negative triggered this firing is owned by the open
record `validate_handoff_crash_and_blockers_shape`, whose file_scope is deliberately disjoint
from this one (it takes `validate-handoff.sh`, the handoff schema and the lean hard agent
instruction; it takes neither file this record owns).

### 550. Probe the Lean LSP index state at dispatch start and propagate the degraded evidence tier downstream
- **Effort**: medium
- **Status**: [NOT STARTED]
- **Task Type**: meta
- **Topic**: agent-system
- **Dependencies**: None

**Description**: Make a cold or unavailable Lean LSP index a measured, propagated condition instead of a notice the
research round observes and nothing downstream ever learns.

EDIT TARGET, binding. Per rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md this repository's `.claude/`
tree is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from a source store; a hand-authored
file landing under `.claude/**` is silently wiped by the next regeneration. Make every edit under
the source store at the mirroring path. RE-DERIVE the store rather than trusting this note, but
know what re-derivation currently yields: the rule says to read `source_dir` from
`<project-root>/.claude-extensions.json`, and that file DOES carry it -- per-extension, at
`.extensions.<name>.source_dir`, not as a top-level key. All seven loaded extensions (core, lean,
formal, typst, memory, literature, filetypes) resolve to
`/home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/<name>`, so the store root is
`/home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system` and resolution works exactly as the rule documents.
Re-derive the path for the extension you are editing with:
  jq -r '.extensions.core.source_dir' .claude-extensions.json
A top-level `jq -r '.source_dir'` returns null and must not be read as the key being absent; that
mistake is what produced an earlier claim of a missing key. If `source_dir` is
still absent when this task runs, record that as an observation of its own rather than silently
hand-authoring under `.claude/**`.

MEASURED {task 836, entry_id iss_1793666803790_QXkGkm}. `lean_local_search` reported
`index: unavailable` for this project at research-dispatch start (phase `research`, dispatch_seq 2),
so every existence and absence claim in that research round is grep-backed rather than LSP-backed.
Per the MCP contract an empty `lean_local_search` result is proof of absence ONLY when its `index`
field says `consulted`; under `unavailable` or `warming` the search never happened, so absence was
never established.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS -- DO NOT REBUILD IT. `extensions/lean/scripts/lean-mcp-preflight-check.sh
--dispatch-block` is already called unconditionally and already injects a
`<lean-readiness-context>` block into Lean dispatches, and that block already carries both a
REACHABILITY tier (`reachable` / `not_reachable` / `unknown`) and the full three-state `index`
interpretation rule, ending with the instruction to "Proceed, but announce this evidence tier
rather than treating a degraded or unavailable index" as proof of absence.
`context/project/lean4/tools/mcp-tools-guide.md`'s `lean_local_search` subsection already carries
the same three-state table and already tells the agent to check for the readiness block before its
first call. So this is NOT a documentation gap and NOT a missing readiness block.

THE ACTUAL GAP, TWO PARTS:
  1. The probe measures REACHABILITY, never index STATE. A server can be reachable while its index
     is `unavailable` or `warming` -- which is what the cited research round hit -- so the injected
     tier was silent about the condition that actually degraded the evidence. The injected prose
     explains how to interpret an `index` value the probe never obtains.
  2. Nothing carries the degraded tier OUT of the research round. The research agent did announce
     it -- the cited issue record is that announcement -- and the downstream planner received no
     machine-readable signal, so a plan was built on grep-backed absence claims with no indication
     they were weaker than LSP-backed ones.

DECIDE AND RECORD, both questions, with the rejected option stated:
  - Should the preflight WARM the index, or only CLASSIFY it? Warming must be bounded against the
     hook's absolute existing contract, which this record must not weaken: always exits 0, always
     emits exactly one line of valid JSON, WARN-never-BLOCK, silent on success, and degrades every
     failure path to a silent empty object rather than non-JSON noise. The `--dispatch-block`
     mode's measured non-Lean early exit of ~6ms is also a cost baseline to respect.
  - What is the propagation carrier for the degraded tier: a field in the research return metadata,
     an explicit statement in the research report, or both? Name the consumer that reads it.

ALSO SETTLE: whether `extensions/lean/hooks/lean-lsp-register-project.sh`'s own documented
session-start snapshot trap -- "a SessionStart hook's own write is NOT reliably visible within the
SAME session that performed it" -- is a contributing cause of `index: unavailable` on a first call,
or an unrelated mechanism. State the finding either way; a negative finding here is a useful result,
not a dead end.

SCOPE BOUND, deliberate: no new context file, and no edit to `extensions/lean/manifest.json` or
`extensions/lean/index-entries.json`. Task 810 holds `extensions/lean/manifest.json` and task 785
holds `extensions/lean/index-entries.json` in their own declared `file_scope`; this record stays
off that territory on purpose. If the chosen design turns out to require a new context file and
therefore index wiring, STOP and raise it rather than taking the overlap.

=== ITEM 1 -- A PLAN'S DECLARED CONTINGENCY FILE IS NEVER HARVESTED ===

MEASURED {task 836, entry_id iss_1793680230317_j91ffI}. A plan declared a Scope Hypothesis
contingency -- move the type lemmas to `LadderPumpType.lean` once `LadderPump.lean` passes 1,000
lines. The implementation took that contingency. `git-commit-scoped.sh` then dropped
`FormalSystem/Metalogic/Decidability/RaySummary/LadderPumpType.lean` from the commit pathspec as
not contained in that task's declared `file_scope`, and the split had to be reverted (commit
`54ba68cc4`). That is real rework caused by a harvesting gap, not by a bad implementation
decision.

THE EXCLUSION IS DELIBERATE AND DOCUMENTED, NOT AN OVERSIGHT. `plan-file-scope-harvest.sh`'s own
header grammar states it outright: "`**Scope Hypothesis**:` is deliberately never treated as a
second harvest source (see plan-format.md's 'Counts-are-hypotheses obligation'
cross-reference) -- only the `Files to modify` block above is read." So this record must SETTLE a
design question, not patch a parser. The two candidate resolutions:

  (a) Scope Hypothesis contingency paths become a second harvest source, and the
      counts-are-hypotheses rationale is amended to say why a contingency PATH is not a
      contingency COUNT.
  (b) `plan-format.md` gains an authoring obligation: a Scope Hypothesis that names a file must
      also list that file in the owning phase's `Files to modify`. The harvester already supports
      this with no code change -- the same header records that it "never stats, resolves, or
      filesystem-validates a harvested path" precisely so that "a path a plan names for a file it
      will CREATE is exactly what must be harvested, not filtered out."

Pick one, implement it, and record the rejected alternative on its own merits.

=== ITEM 2 -- THE SAME DROP, ON A FILE NO PHASE WOULD NAME ===

MEASURED {task 836, entry_id iss_1793678719709_NIgfxx} and {task 836, entry_id
iss_1793679130246_5z9d25}. `git-commit-scoped.sh` dropped `scripts/nolints.json` from a commit
pathspec twice in the same session, for the same containment reason. That file holds four
`unusedArguments` exemption rows for hypotheses the task's pinned Goal signatures carry but their
proofs do not read -- a legitimate, intended modification that no per-phase `Files to modify`
list would plausibly have anticipated.

CURRENT STATE, verify before acting: the file was still uncommitted in the working tree at
`/home/benjamin/Projects/BimodalLogic/scripts/nolints.json` when this record was created
(`git status --short scripts/nolints.json` reported ` M`). Committing it is NOT this record's
deliverable and must not be done under a record scoped as a source-store change. If it is still
uncommitted when this task runs, raise it rather than committing it.

=== THE TWO DECISIONS THIS RECORD OWES ===

Both were named explicitly in the originating change request and both must be answered, with the
rejected option recorded:

  1. Should V10's drop-and-warn posture additionally surface an explicit `proposed_file_scope`
     follow-up rather than only warning? Today a V10 drop produces a WARN textually distinct from
     the other drop classes, an entry in the dedicated `containment_dropped` ledger, and one
     non-fatal `issue-record.sh --class "scope excursion"` call -- which is exactly how the three
     citations above exist at all. The warning is therefore working as designed; the question is
     whether a warning is a sufficient terminus for a drop that silently changes what a commit
     contains.
  2. Should a lint-ledger file like `scripts/nolints.json` belong in a default-permitted scope?
     Note that V10's effective scope is ALREADY wider than the bare declared array: it admits the
     task's own resolved directory, the two fixed literals `specs/TODO.md` and `specs/state.json`,
     and every declared derived-output prefix from `lib/derived-artifact-probe-lib.sh`'s
     `derived_probe_output_prefixes`. So this is a question about extending an existing widening
     mechanism, not about inventing one.

=== CONSTRAINTS ===

NOT a data-repair record. V10's unconditional fail-open posture (on a missing `--task`, a missing
state entry, a malformed `file_scope`, or any internal resolution error), its `issue-record.sh`
call, and the derived-output widening are all correct as they stand. Do NOT weaken V10 into a
refusal: its documented posture is drop-and-warn, never refuse, and the exit-7 observability path
depends on the commit still succeeding. Do not disturb V6's partial-drop gate or V9's
out-of-repository classification; both share the `dropped_pathspecs` ledger with V10 by design and
the header explains why each keeps its own separate array.

VERIFICATION: extend `tests/test-plan-file-scope-harvest.sh` and `tests/test-git-commit-scoped.sh`
rather than replacing them. A regression case reproducing the LadderPumpType drop from a plan
fixture is the minimum bar for item 1.

WHAT THE IMPLEMENTER DID INSTEAD, and why it is the wrong shape. Because the deployed script has
NO `--allow-out-of-scope` flag, and because the V10 containment guard is `--task` opt-in and
FAIL-OPEN when the scope array is empty, the five paths were committed in a SECOND commit with

is strictly worse than an explicit, recorded override: the commit loses its task attribution and

NAMED REMEDY FOR ITEM 2, to be weighed rather than adopted uncritically: add an explicit

out-of-scope paths, and records the excursion (the issue log already has a `scope excursion`
class, and `--honest-index-rows` is precedent for a flag that changes what a commit asserts about
itself). The point is to make the honest path cheaper than the fail-open path.

### 547. Confirm the blocker-research aux carrier landed, and refuse an implement re-dispatch when a plan revision is owed
- **Effort**: high
- **Status**: [NOT STARTED]
- **Task Type**: meta
- **Topic**: agent-system
- **Dependencies**: Task 543

**Description**: Close ONE mechanism that produced two separately-reported defect classes: the orchestrate aux chain's blocker-research carrier is written on instruction alone and never confirmed, and nothing in the dispatch-admission path refuses an implement round for a task that is owed a plan revision.

THE TWO ITEMS ARE ONE RECORD BECAUSE THEY ARE ONE CHAIN, NOT MERELY ONE FILE. Item 1 breaks the carrier that the chain's plan-revision hop depends on; item 2 is the absence of any backstop that would notice. Either alone leaves the observed failure reachable: fixing item 1 without item 2 leaves every OTHER way of losing the hop unguarded, and fixing item 2 without item 1 converts a wasted implement round into a stalled task. They also share `scripts/orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh` territory, which the batching guardrail in `.claude/CLAUDE.md` names as a reason to batch rather than separate.

=== THE MECHANISM, MEASURED IN THE SOURCE STORE DURING THE CREATION OF THIS RECORD -- RE-DERIVE IT RATHER THAN TRUSTING THIS ACCOUNT, WHICH IS A SNAPSHOT OF A ~2400-LINE SCRIPT ===

The chain has four hops, and each is in a different file:

  (1) `scripts/orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh` records the signal: `.aux_pending[t] = {kind: "blocker-research", blocker_desc}`.
  (2) `scripts/orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh`'s AUX CHAIN block reads `aux_pending[t]`, emits a `blocker-research` aux row (agent `fork`), checks `blocker_escalation_count[t]` against `MAX_BLOCKER_ESCALATIONS`, and sets `aux_clear_pending[t]="true"` -- THE PENDING ENTRY IS CLEARED AT EMISSION TIME, before anything confirms the fork did anything.
  (3) `scripts/orchestrate-build-aux-dispatch.sh` builds the fork's prompt, which INSTRUCTS it to "Write compact JSON to '${TASK_DIR_ABS}/.blocker-research.json' with fields: summary (string), root_cause (string), solution_path (string)".
  (4) A LATER cycle's AUX CHAIN block tests `[ -f "$aux_blocker_file" ] && jq empty "$aux_blocker_file"`; on success it emits the `plan-revision` row (`revision_reason=blocker`, agent `reviser-agent`), resolves the latest plan path, and sets `aux_consume_blocker_file[t]="true"` so the carrier is removed. The chain comment states that this chain hop "always produces a `plan-revision` row".

THE FAILURE IS A DEAD DROP WITH NO RECEIPT. If the fork at hop (3) returns without writing the file, hop (2) has ALREADY discarded the pending entry and hop (4)'s file test fails, so NO cycle ever emits the plan-revision row. The task falls through to ordinary status-derived routing and receives another implement dispatch into the phase already known to be blocked. `MAX_BLOCKER_ESCALATIONS` is never approached, because `blocker_escalation_count[t]` advances on the signal being RE-RECORDED rather than on a round failing to produce anything -- so the loop guard that exists cannot see this shape of loop.

ONE CONTRAST WORTH CARRYING INTO THE FIX, because it shows the system already knows the difference. The `plan-revision` prompt in the same `case` statement of the same file ends with: "Do this every time, unconditionally, even if you cannot tell whether an implement dispatch for this task is live this cycle", and points at `context/patterns/plan-revision-notification.md` for the sentinel's full contract. The `blocker-research` prompt carries no such insistence and no contract pointer. That asymmetry is not obviously deliberate and the research phase should settle whether it is.

=== ITEM 1 -- THE CARRIER WRITE IS INSTRUCTED BUT NEVER VERIFIED ===

MEASURED, in the originating run: a plan phase named `specs/{NNN}_{SLUG}/.blocker-research.json` as the artifact to CORRECT, in order to retire a stale route recommendation it was said to hold. No such file existed when the phase ran. The concurrent aux blocker-research dispatch produced no artifact, so the recommendation the plan wanted retired had no on-disk carrier, and the task was skipped as a recorded deviation.

A TRAP THIS SETS FOR THE IMPLEMENTER, STATED SO IT IS NOT WALKED INTO. That path EXISTS in the originating task directory now -- it was written later in the same orchestration by a subsequent dispatch. Do NOT reproduce the defect by checking that one path, finding a file, and concluding the mechanism is sound. The observable to reproduce is a blocker-research aux round that RETURNS WITHOUT WRITING, which is a fork-behaviour condition, not a property of any particular task directory. Drive it from a test that stubs the aux dispatch rather than from live evidence.

THREE REMEDY SHAPES, NONE PRE-COMMITTED; DECIDE IN RESEARCH AND RECORD THE REASON:

  (a) CONFIRM-THEN-CLEAR. Do not clear `aux_pending[t]` until the carrier is confirmed present and parseable, so the next cycle re-emits. This needs a bound against unbounded re-emission, and the obvious bound -- `blocker_escalation_count[t]` -- currently increments at a different point in the flow than this remedy needs; settle where it must increment, and say what happens at the cap.
  (b) SYNTHESIZE A MINIMAL CARRIER from the aux fork's own return payload when the fork wrote none, so hop (4) still fires with whatever the fork actually reported. This preserves the chain at the cost of a carrier whose provenance differs from the documented one; if chosen, the synthesized shape must be distinguishable from a fork-written one by anything that reads it.
  (c) FAIL LOUD. Treat an absent carrier as a hard escalation: surface the task in `blocked[]` with a reason naming the absent path and the aux round that should have produced it, and let a human decide.

WHATEVER IS CHOSEN, THE MINIMUM BAR IS AUDIBILITY. Today the absence is silent in every channel -- no stderr notice, no issue-log entry, no `blocked[]` row, no state field. A reader of the run cannot tell a chain that completed from a chain that evaporated. Any landed remedy must leave the absence detectable from the run's own output.

=== ITEM 2 -- NOTHING REFUSES AN IMPLEMENT DISPATCH WHEN A PLAN REVISION IS OWED ===

MEASURED THREE TIMES, across two orchestration sessions. Two dispatches resumed a phase from `[BLOCKED]` with no intervening plan revision. A third was an implement dispatch although the preceding handoff's own recorded immediate next action was a PLAN REVISION. The effect each time was an implement round entering a phase already known to be blocked and re-deriving the blocker instead of advancing.

MEASURED IN THE SOURCE STORE, AND THIS IS THE LOAD-BEARING FINDING: the staleness check exists, but on the WRONG SIDE of the dispatch. The `.plan-revised.json` sentinel's `revised_at` field appears in `scripts/orchestrate-build-aux-dispatch.sh`, `context/patterns/plan-revision-notification.md`, `agents/general-implementation-agent.md` and `agents/reviser-agent.md` -- and in NO code path of `scripts/orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh`. The implementation agent compares `revised_at` against `dispatch_start_ts` AFTER it has already been dispatched; the planner that decides WHETHER to dispatch never consults the sentinel at all. An in-agent check can therefore only report the wasted round, never prevent it. That is exactly what the originating run shows: the sentinel's `revised_at` predated `dispatch_start_ts` and the round proceeded anyway.

MEASURED, ON HOW A `blocked` CANDIDATE IS READMITTED -- the two engines differ and the difference matters. `scripts/orchestrate-triage-classify.sh`'s own routing table routes a DISCHARGED `blocked` candidate (all `dependencies[]` completed, no handoff blockers) by its `previous_status`, so a task whose `previous_status` was `implementing` re-enters the implement arm; `needs_human` is reserved for the non-discharged cases. The inline fallback table inside `orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh` maps `blocked` unconditionally to `needs_human`. So it is the live classifier's DISCHARGE path that readmits implement, and the fallback would not have. Any fix must be made in the live engine and the fallback kept in lockstep with it -- that file's own comments state the two tables must agree, and `tests/test-orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh` already carries a parity fixture asserting it.

THE HOOK ALREADY EXISTS, PARTLY. The classifier already reads `.orchestrator-handoff.json` for a `blocked` or `partial` candidate and already extracts `blocker_count`, `continuation_ok` and `age_min`. It reads whether blockers are present and whether the continuation pointer is valid -- NOT what the handoff says the next action is.

AND HERE IS THE CONSTRAINT THAT MAKES THIS A DECISION RATHER THAN AN EDIT. `context/schemas/orchestrator-handoff-schema.json` does carry a `next_action_hint` field, but its schema reads in full: `{"type": "string", "description": "Optional short hint describing the immediate next step for a resuming dispatch."}`. It is OPTIONAL and FREE TEXT, it is not in the schema's `required` list, and it is consumed by NO routing code -- its only source-store readers are `scripts/validate-handoff.sh`, `scripts/tests/test-handoff-reader-parity.sh`, `docs/architecture/handoff-schema.md` and `context/patterns/system-defect-discrimination.md`. A routing predicate CANNOT soundly key on free prose; a substring match for "revis" would be a guess dressed as a mechanism. Choose deliberately among:

  (i) Give `next_action_hint` a constrained vocabulary (or add a sibling enum field) so a router can read it. This is a handoff-schema change and obliges updating the schema, `docs/architecture/handoff-schema.md`, `validate-handoff.sh` and every writer that emits a handoff -- a real cost to state before choosing it.
  (ii) Key the predicate on CHAIN STATE instead of on handoff prose: a task with an outstanding blocker-research or plan-revision obligation is recorded in the multi-task state file, which the planner already reads. This needs no schema change and is the cheaper shape, and it composes with item 1's remedy -- note that it also DEPENDS on item 1, because today the obligation is erased at emission time.
  (iii) Key it on the sentinel directly: a `blocked`/`partial` candidate whose `previous_status` was `implementing` is not implement-eligible unless `.plan-revised.json` exists with `revised_at >= dispatch_start_ts` of the dispatch that blocked it. This moves the EXISTING check to the right side of the dispatch and is the smallest change, but it must not deadlock a task for which no revision was ever owed.

FORCING FLAGS MUST KEEP WORKING, AND THIS IS AN ACCEPTANCE CONDITION, NOT A FOOTNOTE. An explicit `/orchestrate --implement` override admits one dispatch deliberately; `/orchestrate --research|--plan|--implement` is also the documented admit-once path for a held task. The new predicate MUST NOT silently defeat an explicit override. State in the landed prose what an override does against an owed plan revision -- admit with a warning is the expected answer, but it must be stated and tested rather than left to the reader.

=== SIBLING RECORD -- CROSS-REFERENCE, DO NOT RESTATE, NO DEPENDENCY EDGE ===

The record `plan_self_consistency_and_artifact_existence` owns the plan-AUTHORING half of item 1's same observation: that a plan must not make a phase goal turn on a dispatch-created orchestration sidecar, and must name the durable record as the carrier instead. It cites the same originating issue entry. That record explicitly forbids itself from changing any script's behaviour; THIS record owns the script half and must not restate that record's prose. The two touch disjoint files and may land in either order, so no edge is declared between them. Read it before writing any prose here, so the two do not contradict each other on what the sanctioned carrier is.

The edge carries no claim that this record needs that one's content.

### 546. Diagnose the zero-result literature retrieval and settle the degraded-signal contract
- **Effort**: medium
- **Status**: [NOT STARTED]
- **Task Type**: meta
- **Topic**: agent-system
- **Dependencies**: None

**Description**: Diagnose why a ranked literature query over indexed material returned nothing, and settle the `degraded` field's contract on an empty result set. Two coupled items in `literature-search.sh`, which must be investigated together: item 2 is the signal that misled the caller about item 1, and item 2's correct remedy depends on what item 1 turns out to be.

NOTHING IN THE CORPUS IS BROKEN AND THIS IS NOT A DATA-REPAIR RECORD. The deliverable is a fix (or, for item 2, a possibly documentation-only correction) in the literature extension's source store. Do NOT re-ingest, re-convert or re-chunk any source as part of this record; if the diagnosis concludes that a reindex is required, state that conclusion and raise it rather than performing a corpus operation under a record scoped as a script fix.

=== ITEM 1 -- A RANKED QUERY RETURNED NOTHING FOR MATERIAL THAT IS PRESENT ===

MEASURED, in the originating run: `literature-search.sh` returned `degraded=true` with ZERO results for a query about the HWZ quasimodel construction. The caller worked around it by grepping the corpus source directory directly for `Theorem 14` and `Definition 12`, and found the material. So the content was reachable by substring search at the moment the ranked search reported nothing.

MEASURED FRESH DURING THE CREATION OF THIS RECORD, not copied from the originating run: this repository's `specs/literature-index.json` holds 106 entries and contains both the token `HWZ` and the token `quasimodel` (the latter at several entries). The material is therefore NOT absent from this repository's literature sub-index.

THE DISCRIMINATION THE DIAGNOSIS MUST MAKE FIRST, BEFORE ANY FIX. The sub-index and the ranked search read DIFFERENT STORES. `specs/literature-index.json` is per-repo metadata; the ranked search reads an FTS5 full-text database over converted chunk files. Presence in the former is not evidence of presence in the latter, and the measurement above establishes only the former. Settle, in this order, which of these is the actual cause before changing any code:

  (a) The chunks for that source were never indexed into the FTS5 database, or the database is stale with respect to them -- a coverage/freshness problem, whose fix is not in this script at all.
  (b) The chunks are indexed but the query did not match them -- a tokenization, query-construction or ranking problem, whose fix may be in this script.
  (c) The query raised an FTS5 error that was swallowed into an empty result rather than surfaced -- note that the envelope carries a `query_error` field precisely for this, so check whether it was populated and, if it was, why the caller did not see it.

Report which of (a), (b) or (c) it was. If it is (a), this record's item 1 deliverable is that finding plus whatever authoring or diagnostic guidance prevents the next caller from reading a coverage gap as a tool failure -- NOT a speculative change to the ranking code.

=== ITEM 2 -- `degraded` CARRIES NO INFORMATION EXACTLY WHEN THE RESULT SET IS EMPTY ===

MEASURED in the deployed copy, at THREE separate envelope-construction sites (the single-query builder and two others; locate all three by searching for the assignment, and fix or document all three rather than the first one found -- line numbers drift and are not durable anchors). Every site has the same shape:

    if merged:
        ... fallback_tier = 'bm25' | 'phrase_retry' | 'trigram' | 'none'
    else:
        fallback_tier = 'none'
    degraded = fallback_tier != 'bm25'

On an empty result set `fallback_tier` is unconditionally `'none'`, so `degraded` is unconditionally `true`. A genuine zero-result query and a retrieval-degraded zero-result query are therefore INDISTINGUISHABLE in the envelope: both report `degraded=true, fallback_tier='none'`.

THIS CONTRADICTS THE FIELD'S OWN DOCUMENTED CONTRACT. The comment sitting immediately above the first of those sites states that `degraded` "is the honest, never-silent signal that distinguishes 'retrieval degraded' from 'genuine zero-result'". The code cannot make that distinction. Whatever else this record does, that comment and the code must be brought into agreement -- either by making the code deliver what the comment promises, or by correcting the comment. Leaving a comment that overpromises a field's meaning is what produced the originating confusion.

CONSUMER SCOPE, MEASURED -- AND ONE PASSAGE THAT MUST NOT BE "FIXED". `literature-briefing.sh` gates its `[DEGRADED RETRIEVAL - fallback_tier: ...]` banner on `degraded` being true AND the briefing line array being NON-EMPTY. The briefing path is therefore ALREADY guarded against the tautology above and never shows a degraded banner on a zero-result query. Do not change that gate: it is correct as it stands, and an implementer who "fixes" it will be removing the one guard that works. The unguarded consumer is any caller that reads the raw envelope JSON directly, which is exactly what the originating run did.

THE REMEDY IS A CHOICE, NOT A FOREGONE CONCLUSION -- MAKE IT IN RESEARCH, WITH THE CONSUMERS ENUMERATED. Two defensible shapes, and the decision must be recorded with its reason:

  - Make the value honest: report `degraded=false` when the result set is empty and `query_error` is null (a genuine zero-result), reserving `degraded=true` for a real degradation. This CHANGES THE FIELD'S VALUE for existing callers and is therefore an interface change -- enumerate every consumer of `degraded` and `fallback_tier` across the source store before choosing it, including the legacy bare-array envelope shape the briefing script still accepts.
  - Keep the value and correct the contract: document that `degraded` is meaningful only when `results` is non-empty, and state the rule a raw-JSON consumer should use instead -- most plausibly that an empty `results` with a null `query_error` is a genuine zero-result, while a non-null `query_error` is a hard failure.

Whichever is chosen, a raw-JSON caller must be left with a stated, checkable rule for telling "nothing matched" from "retrieval broke". That is the actual deliverable of item 2.

=== WHY THE TWO ITEMS ARE ONE RECORD ===

Item 2 alone does not explain item 1, and fixing item 2 in isolation would be the worse outcome of the two: a tidied flag reporting an honest `degraded=false` on a query that STILL returns nothing for material that is present would retire the only signal that anything was wrong, while leaving the retrieval failure untouched and harder to notice next time. Item 1 is the primary; item 2 is the reason the caller misread it. Settle item 1 first.

=== DEPENDENCY EDGE, AND WHY IT IS AN EDGE RATHER THAN AN EXCLUSION ===

`agent-system/extensions/literature/scripts/literature-search.sh` is already claimed by the open grouped defect record `agent_system_batch_defect_group`, whose own `file_scope` lists this exact path and whose DEFECT 4 fixes the `--read` chunk-file path resolution in the same script. ### 545. Report a reversed validate-artifact.sh invocation as an argument-order fault, not a missing file
- **Effort**: low
- **Status**: [NOT STARTED]
- **Task Type**: meta
- **Topic**: agent-system
- **Dependencies**: None

**Description**: Make `validate-artifact.sh` report an argument-order fault as an argument-order fault, instead of as a missing file that does not exist.

MEASURED. The script's contract is `validate-artifact.sh <artifact_path> <type> [--fix] [--strict]`, with `<type>` one of `report`, `plan`, `summary`. Invoked in the reversed order it fails with `[FAIL] File not found: report` and exit 3 -- naming the TYPE as though it were a path. The reader is pointed at a filesystem problem that does not exist: a path they never passed, reported absent, while the real fault is positional. No deliverable was affected; the re-run in the documented order passed with 0 warnings. The cost is diagnostic misdirection, which is why the severity is minor and the fix should stay small.

WHY IT HAPPENS. The guard sequence in `agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/validate-artifact.sh` is: a both-arguments-non-empty check (empty either side prints the usage line and exits 4), then `[ ! -f "$artifact_path" ]` (exit 3, the observed message), then `[ ! -s "$artifact_path" ]` (exit 1), and only then the `case "$artifact_type"` dispatch whose `*)` arm prints `[FAIL] Unknown artifact type: ... (expected: report, plan, summary)`. A reversed invocation passes the non-empty check with both slots filled, then dies on the file test before the type test is ever reached. The type-validation arm that could have named the real fault is downstream of the file test that cannot.

NOTE THE NEAR-MISS REMEDY. Merely moving the `case` dispatch ahead of the file-existence test does NOT fix this. On a reversed invocation the type slot holds the PATH, so the type check would fire with `[FAIL] Unknown artifact type: specs/.../01_foo.md (expected: report, plan, summary)` -- a different misdirection, not a correction. The fault must be detected as a swap, not inferred from one slot in isolation.

DESIGN SPACE. Two options, both acceptable; the change request approved either:
  (a) ACCEPT EITHER ORDER. Detect the swap -- the second argument is not one of the three type keywords while the first argument is -- and transparently swap the two before validating. Permissive and friction-free, at the cost of making the documented argument order advisory in practice; if chosen, decide whether to emit an advisory note on the swapped path or stay silent, and say which in the summary.
  (b) NAME THE REAL FAULT. Keep the documented order strict, but detect the same swap condition and fail with a message that says so -- argument order reversed, expected `<artifact_path> <type>`, naming both received values -- rather than reporting a phantom missing file. If a new exit code is introduced for this, treat it as a vocabulary change and check the existing consumers of exits 1, 3 and 4 first; reusing 4 (the usage/arity code) is the natural choice and needs no new vocabulary.
Whichever is chosen, the detection predicate must handle the genuinely ambiguous cases deliberately rather than by accident: both arguments being type keywords, neither being one (which should keep today's behaviour -- a real missing-file report is correct then), and a real file on disk literally named `report`, `plan`, or `summary`.

OVERLAP -- CROSS-REPO ONLY, AND NOTHING MECHANICAL WILL CATCH IT. No record in this repository claims this script. The source-store repository (~/.config/nvim) maintains its own task space that no dependency edge or file_scope gate can reach, and two records there are not_started and claim `agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/validate-artifact.sh`: `validate_that_every_carried_unverified_mark_names_a_source` and `extend_the_carried_figure_obligation_to_a_recommendations_mechanical_claim`. The second also claims `agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/test-validate-artifact.sh`, the test suite this record must extend. Both are about CARRIED-UNVERIFIED mark validation -- a different concern from argument parsing, so there is no duplication of substance and neither record subsumes this one. Re-derive their state at implement time rather than trusting this snapshot, read whatever has landed, and coordinate rather than racing. Because the overlap cannot be expressed as a dependency across repositories, this coordination is a human obligation, not a gated one.

ACCEPTANCE.
  (1) A reversed invocation no longer reports a missing file. It either succeeds (option a) or fails with a message naming argument order as the fault (option b).
  (2) The chosen option is recorded with its reasoning, and the rejected one on its own merits.
  (3) The ambiguous cases enumerated above each have a decided, tested behaviour -- in particular, a genuinely missing path with a valid type still reports `File not found` at exit 3, unchanged.
  (4) `agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/test-validate-artifact.sh` reports zero failures, with a failing-first case for the reversed invocation. Demonstrate it fails against the source-store script before the fix.
  (5) The usage line at the top of the script and its header comment agree with the implemented behaviour. If option (a) is chosen, the usage line must not imply the order is mandatory.
  (6) The deployed tree is not hand-authored. The edit lands in `agent-system/extensions/core/**` and reaches `.claude/**` only by deploy.

DELIVERABLE PROSE CONSTRAINTS. The edited files lie outside `specs/**`: no task-number references (`.claude/rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md`) and no record-versioning language (`.claude/rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md`). Durable anchors citable freely: the script name `validate-artifact.sh`, the flag spellings (`--fix`, `--strict`), the type keywords (`report`, `plan`, `summary`), the exit codes (`1`, `3`, `4`), and the message texts themselves. MUST NOT appear: the originating task number, the issue entry_id, and the specific artifact path from the measured run.

PROVENANCE. Raised during orchestration and approved at the orchestrate-lead level as an agent-system change request, dispatched through the conclusion stage's agent-system channel. Originating entry: {task: 820, entry_id: iss_1792347398463_OSs9p5}, class `tooling`, severity `minor`, phase `research`, in specs/820_*/issues.jsonl. No `suggested_channel` hint was carried, so there is no hint-versus-decision override to record.

### 544. Make a fixture-dependent Lean gate statement expressible and mechanically checkable in a plan Challenge block
- **Effort**: medium
- **Status**: [NOT STARTED]
- **Task Type**: meta
- **Topic**: agent-system
- **Dependencies**: Task 539

**Description**: Give the Lean Challenge-pinning mechanism a way to express and mechanically check a gate statement that depends on a model-layer fixture. Today such a statement cannot be pinned at all, and the workaround in use -- a per-phase "Target statement" line in prose -- is checked by nothing.

MEASURED MECHANISM. `agent-system/extensions/lean/scripts/lean-challenge-snapshot.sh` forces EVERY matched declaration body to `sorry` when it assembles the standalone challenge module. The declaration regex (`DECL_RE`, the `(?:theorem|lemma|def|instance)` alternation) matches `def` as well as `theorem`, so a fixture `def` is not exempt: its body is replaced too, by the same `head + " := sorry"` rewrite at the body-forcing assembler, and again at the git-pinned signature reader's own `header + " := sorry"` site. The consequence to confirm against the script before designing the fix: a fixture `def` reduced to `sorry` no longer carries the model it defined, so a gate theorem whose statement mentions that fixture cannot elaborate standalone in the assembled module, and the whole pin attempt fails rather than the one statement degrading. Verify the precise failure mode -- whether elaboration fails on the fixture `def` itself (an unannotated `:= sorry` has no inferrable type) or downstream on the theorem's own statement -- since the two admit different remedies and the design choice depends on which it is.

THE WORKAROUND, AND WHY IT IS UNENFORCED. The approach actually used was to pin only the fixture-free generic theorems in the plan's `## Lean Challenge Statements` block, and to record each fixture-level gate theorem's intended signature per phase under a "Target statement" line, naming the statement-fidelity obligation in prose. That split is sound as a plan-authoring judgment and should not be condemned; the defect is that it has no contract and no check. The string "Target statement" appears NOWHERE in the source store's context or rules trees -- not in `plan-format.md`, not in `challenge-snapshot.md`, not in `plan-compliance.md` -- so it is private ad-hoc prose, carrying none of the standing a pinned block carries and verified by nothing. A pinned statement is diffed declaration-by-declaration; a Target statement line is read by a human or not at all.

DESIGN SPACE -- DECIDE, DO NOT ASSUME. At least three shapes are available and the record deliberately does not pick one:
  (a) Exempt fixture declarations from body-forcing, so the assembled module retains enough of the model layer for a fixture-dependent statement to elaborate. This is the most direct fix and the most invasive: it weakens the "every body is `sorry`" invariant the script's own comment asserts, and the reason that invariant exists (a challenge module must not smuggle in a proof) must be re-established for whatever carve-out is chosen. An opt-in marker on the fixture, rather than a blanket `def` exemption, is likely the narrower form.
  (b) Promote "Target statement" from prose to a recognised plan-format construct with its own mechanical check -- a declaration-by-declaration signature diff against the implemented declaration, with the same advisory standing `--check` has. This leaves the script's sorry invariant untouched and makes the workaround enforceable as-is.
  (c) Allow a pinned statement to declare its fixture dependencies explicitly, so the snapshot can assemble a module that includes them unforced while still forcing every theorem body.
Choose on the merits during the plan round, state the reasoning, and record the rejected options on their own merits.

SECONDARY ANGLE -- SAME TOOL, AND LARGELY ALREADY OWNED ELSEWHERE. At implement time `lean-challenge-snapshot.sh --check` was unavailable: it exited 71 because no snapshot had been taken at plan time, so even the pinned generic statements were verified only by a hand token-by-token comparison against the plan. CORRECT THE FRAMING BEFORE ACTING ON IT: the failure is not silent. The script prints `ERROR: no manifest found at <path> -- run the snapshot (without --check) first.` to stderr before exiting. The real deficiencies are that exit 71 is overloaded (it is also the identifier-set-mismatch code and the catch-all config-error code, at several distinct sites), and that nothing at plan time makes the snapshot prerequisite visible before `--check` is written into a Verification criterion. BOTH of those are already owned by #813 `State the precedence and snapshot-prerequisite rules for a lean plan's pinned Challenge block` [not_started], whose item 2 states the prerequisite rule in both directions, names the declaration-by-declaration diff as the sanctioned self-contained substitute, and adds the no-manifest case to the exit-code table's 71 row -- while explicitly binding itself NOT to change the script. Do not re-do that work here and do not close either record as a duplicate of the other. The residue genuinely left to this record is the tooling question that record forbade itself: whether the script should distinguish no-manifest from identifier-mismatch at all, and if so how, given that a new exit code is a vocabulary change with its own consumers. Treat that as a scoped decision with "leave the exit code alone, the contract fix suffices" as a legitimate outcome -- in which case say so in the completion summary rather than leaving it unaddressed.

OVERLAP ON THESE SAME FILES -- TWO RECORDS IN THIS REPO, ONE ACROSS REPOS. Both in-repo records are claimed as dependency edges rather than excluded, because the overlap is unordered and the territory is shared:
  - #768 `lean-challenge-snapshot swallows declarations, mishandles Unicode names, and over-reads Goals prose` [not_started] owns three defects in this same script and touches the same declaration-alternation and body-forcing sites this record must touch. Its record also warns that the source store carries UNCOMMITTED repairs to the script and its test suite plus two untracked fixtures, and that the DEPLOYED copy is stale and will mislead anyone who reads it to establish current behaviour. Read the source store, not the deploy tree, and read that record's landed state first.
  - #813, delimited above, owns `challenge-snapshot.md` and `plan-compliance.md`. If the option chosen here requires a change to the design record `challenge-snapshot.md`, coordinate rather than editing a file another record claims.
  - CROSS-REPO, AND NOTHING MECHANICAL WILL CATCH IT: the source-store repository (~/.config/nvim) holds `lean4_plan_with_zero_lean_goals` [not_started] -- "Define the sanctioned shape for a lean4-typed plan that commits to no theorem, and make lean-challenge-snapshot.sh distinguish it from a malformed one" -- whose file_scope is exactly `agent-system/extensions/core/context/formats/plan-format.md`, `agent-system/extensions/lean/scripts/lean-challenge-snapshot.sh`, and `agent-system/extensions/lean/context/project/lean4/domain/challenge-snapshot.md`. Its subject (a deliberate no-theorem plan being indistinguishable from a malformed one, both exiting 71) is different from this one, but it is the third claimant on the same three files and the two task spaces cannot see each other. Re-derive its state at implement time and coordinate.

ACCEPTANCE.
  (1) The fixture-dependent failure mode has been reproduced against the script as it stands in the SOURCE STORE (including its uncommitted modifications), and the completion summary names which elaboration step actually fails.
  (2) One of the design options is implemented, with the rejected ones recorded on their own merits, and the chosen option states explicitly what remains of the "every theorem body is `sorry`" invariant and why a challenge module still cannot smuggle in a proof.
  (3) A fixture-dependent statement is now expressible AND mechanically checkable -- a change that makes it expressible but still unchecked does not satisfy this record, since unenforceability is the defect.
  (4) `agent-system/extensions/lean/scripts/tests/test-lean-challenge-snapshot.sh` reports zero failures, with a failing-first case covering a gate statement that depends on a fixture declaration. Demonstrate the case fails against the source-store script before the fix, not against the stale deployed copy.
  (5) The secondary angle is dispositioned: either the exit-code distinction is implemented, or the summary records the decision to leave it to the contract-level record and why.
  (6) The deployed tree is not hand-authored. Every edit lands under `agent-system/extensions/lean/**` (or `core/**` if plan-format is touched) and reaches `.claude/**` only by deploy.

DELIVERABLE PROSE CONSTRAINTS. Every edited file lies outside `specs/**`: no task-number references (`.claude/rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md`) and no record-versioning language (`.claude/rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md`). Durable anchors citable freely: the script name `lean-challenge-snapshot.sh`, flag spellings (`--check`, `--force`, `--dry-run`), exit codes (`65`, `71`, `73`), section names (`## Lean Challenge Statements`, `**Goals**:`), the manifest path shape `specs/{NNN}_{SLUG}/challenge/manifest.json`, and neighbouring file names. MUST NOT appear: the originating task number, the issue entry_id, and the specific declaration or fixture names from the measured run -- those live in this record only.

PROVENANCE. Raised during orchestration and approved at the orchestrate-lead level as an agent-system change request, dispatched through the conclusion stage's agent-system channel. Originating entry: {task: 820, entry_id: iss_1792348402766_UnLOsz}, class `planning`, severity `minor`, phase `plan`, in specs/820_*/issues.jsonl. No `suggested_channel` hint was carried, so there is no hint-versus-decision override to record.

FILE_SCOPE IS DELIBERATELY NARROWER THAN THE DESIGN SPACE -- RAISE, DO NOT WIDEN SILENTLY. This record's file_scope names only the script, its test suite and its fixtures directory. It deliberately OMITS `agent-system/extensions/lean/context/project/lean4/domain/challenge-snapshot.md` and `agent-system/extensions/core/context/formats/plan-format.md`, because #813 claims the first and the cross-repo record claims both. Design option (b) in particular -- promoting "Target statement" to a recognised plan-format construct -- cannot be executed without one or both of them. If the chosen option requires either file, RAISE IT at plan time and have the scope widened or the work re-sited by agreement, rather than editing a file another record claims or quietly expanding scope at implement time.
